# GenAI and LLM interview questions with answers: RAG, fine-tuning, prompting, agents, evaluation and system design, from both sides of the table
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/genai-interview-questions/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

What do GenAI engineer interviews actually ask? Six things, in some order: LLM fundamentals, tokens, context, attention, hallucination; RAG, how you build and evaluate retrieval; fine-tuning, when and how with LoRA; prompting and agents, including safety; evaluation and cost, how you know it works and what it costs; and one system design where you assemble the pieces. Plus a walkthrough of a project you built, which is where most decisions get made. Definitions get you past the first minute. Trade-offs and stories get you the offer. Also asked as: genai interview questions · generative ai interview questions · llm interview questions · llm interview questions and answers · genai engineer interview questions · ai engineer interview questions · generative ai interview questions and answers for freshers · llm engineer interview · rag interview questions I have sat on both sides: interviewing candidates for SCULT INDIA and being interviewed for GenAI roles. The pattern is consistent enough that this page is the preparation I now give mentees, with the answers I would want to hear. Longer notes are on the portfolio [11][12]. The question is never really "what is RAG". The question is "have you built one, and do you know what broke". Answer the second question every time. Pranjul Rathour LLM fundamentals: what will they ask? Expect: what is a token and why does it matter for cost; what is the context window and one failure mode of long contexts; explain attention in one minute; what is hallucination and how do you manage it; open-weight versus API models for a given product; what is the difference between a base model and an instruct model. Answer each with the concept in one sentence, then a consequence for a product you built. Also asked as: llm fundamentals interview questions · transformer interview questions · what is a token interview · attention mechanism interview question · hallucination interview question · context window interview question · llm basics interview Fundamentals, and the answer shape that worksQuestionThe one-sentence coreThen sayWhat is a token?The unit the model reads andwrites, a word pieceCost and context limits are intokens, so every prompt designis a token budgetWhat is attention?Every token weighs everyearlier token to decide whatmatters [4]It is why cost grows withcontext lengthWhat is the contextwindow?The maximum tokens in onerequest, prompt plus answerModels use the middle of longcontexts worse [8], soretrieval and reranking stillWhat is hallucination?Fluent output that isunsupported, a property ofnext-token predictionYou manage it with retrieval,constraints and evaluation,not with hopeBase vs instruct model?Base predicts textinstruct was tuned to followrequestsFine-tune from instruct forchat tasks, from base for rawcompletion formatsFundamentals, and the answer shape that works RAG interview questions Expect: explain RAG end to end; why is chunking important and how do you choose a size; why add keyword search to embeddings; what does a reranker do; how do you evaluate retrieval separately from generation; how do you stop the model answering when the documents do not contain the answer; how would you handle multi-tenant documents. Every question maps to a stage of the pipeline; know the pipeline and you know the questions. Also asked as: rag interview questions · rag interview questions and answers · retrieval augmented generation interview · vector database interview questions · embeddings interview questions · chunking interview questions · rag system design interview · rag evaluation interview The RAG walkthrough interviewers want1Ingest and chunk,structure-aware,headings prepended2Embed with one model,store with metadata3Retrieve withembeddings and BM25,fuse the lists4Rerank with a cross-encoder to a handfulof passages5Gate on confidence,refuse weak evidence6Generate withcitations, stream theanswer7Measure recall at kand faithfulness on afixed question setThe RAG walkthrough interviewers want The paper to cite is Lewis et al. [1]; the metric framework most interviewers know is RAGAS [7]. The answer that separates candidates is to the evaluation question: "I measure retrieval recall on twenty labelled questions before I look at a single generated answer, because a system can be faithful to the wrong passage." Fine-tuning interview questions Expect: when would you fine-tune instead of using RAG; explain LoRA and QLoRA; how do you prepare a dataset; how do you read a loss curve; what is catastrophic forgetting; how do you evaluate a fine-tuned model honestly; can you fine-tune GPT. The trap question is "how would you teach the model our product facts", and the right answer is "I would not, I would retrieve them, and fine-tune only for the voice and format". Also asked as: fine tuning interview questions · lora interview questions · qlora interview questions · peft interview questions · fine tuning vs rag interview question · llm training interview questions · instruction tuning interview · rlhf interview questions Fine-tuning questions and the core of each answerQuestionCoreWhen to fine-tune?For behaviour, style, format and narrow skillsafter prompting failsnever for facts that changeWhat is LoRA?Freeze the base, train small low-rank adaptermatrices per layer [2]What is QLoRA?LoRA on a 4-bit quantised basea 7B model fits a free 16 GB GPU [3]Dataset?A spec, clean consistent examples in themodel&#x27;s chat template, a held-out split, asample read by eyeLoss curve?Training fallsvalidation falls then flattensvalidation rising means memorising, roll backForgetting?Narrow training overwrites general abilitylower rates, fewer epochs, mix in general dataEvaluation?Base versus tuned on the same held-outprompts, side by side, scored against the specFine-tuning questions and the core of each answer Prompt engineering and agent interview questions Expect: system prompt versus user prompt and why the split matters for security; what is prompt injection and how do you limit its damage; when does chain-of-thought help and when does it waste tokens; how do you test a prompt; what is an agent and where does the model's judgement actually belong; how would you stop an agent taking a harmful action; when is a workflow better than an agent. Safety questions are where candidates who have only prototyped get exposed. Also asked as: prompt engineering interview questions · ai agent interview questions · agentic ai interview questions · prompt injection interview question · system prompt interview · tool calling interview · llm security interview questions · langchain interview questions The references interviewers respect: chain-of-thought [5], ReAct for agents [6], OWASP for security [9], and Anthropic's guide for the workflow-versus-agent distinction [10]. The answer to "how do you stop a harmful action" is not a clever prompt; it is least-privilege tools and a human confirmation for anything irreversible. A career session for students Evaluation and cost questions Expect: how do you know your system works; what metrics do you track; how do you test a prompt change before deploying; how much does this feature cost per month; how would you cut that cost in half; what do you log. The interviewer is testing whether you treat an LLM system like software. Answer with a fixed evaluation set, metrics per stage, a CI check, tokens logged per request, and a cost model: input plus output tokens times price times requests. Also asked as: llm evaluation interview questions · how to evaluate llm interview · ai cost estimation interview · llm observability interview · llm testing interview · genai production interview questions · mlops for llm interview The evaluation answer, in fullA fixed set of real inputs with expected outputs, grown over timeRetrieval recall at k, measured before generationFaithfulness and relevance on generated answers, model-judged plus human sampleA CI job that runs the set on every prompt or model changeTokens, latency, cost and outcome logged per requestAlerts on error rate, latency and spendA monthly review of failures that becomes the next test casesThe evaluation answer, in full System design questions for GenAI roles Expect one design in 30 to 45 minutes: a support chatbot over company documents, a document extraction service, a coding assistant, a voice assistant for a regional language. Structure it: clarify users and constraints, draw the request path, name each component and its failure mode, say what you would measure, estimate cost, and state what you would cut for version one. Interviewers grade the trade-offs you name unprompted, not the boxes you draw. Also asked as: genai system design interview · llm system design interview questions · design a chatbot interview · rag system design interview · ai system design questions · design an llm application interview · system design for ai engineer How a system design answer is gradedLEVEL 1Boxesnamed components in asensible orderLEVEL 2Flowsthe request path, theindexing path, whereretrieval and generationsitLEVEL 3Failureswhat breaks at eachcomponent and the fixLEVEL 4Measuresrecall, faithfulness,latency, cost, and wherethey are loggedLEVEL 5Judgementwhat you cut for versionone and why, and what youwould add nextHow a system design answer is graded Behavioural and project questions Expect: tell me about a project; what broke and what did you do; a time you disagreed with a technical decision; how you handle a requirement you think is wrong; why this role. For the project question, use one project and go deep: the problem, the decision you made, the failure you hit, the fix, the measured result. My RAG platform's confidence gate exists because of a failure; that story has done more for me in interviews than any definition. Also asked as: tell me about a project interview ai · behavioural interview questions ai engineer · how to explain ai project in interview · how to present portfolio in interview · interview questions about failures · why do you want to work in ai interview My separate note on the "tell me about a project" question, with the structure and a worked example, is on the portfolio [13]. Coding rounds for GenAI roles Expect Python: parse and validate a JSON output against a schema; implement reciprocal rank fusion over two ranked lists; write a retry with backoff around an API call; chunk a text by paragraphs with a size cap; compute cosine similarity; write a small evaluation loop. Rarely leetcode-style puzzles. Write clear, typed, tested code, talk while you write, and handle the edge case out loud. The interviewer is watching how you work, not whether you finish. Also asked as: coding questions for ai engineer interview · python interview questions for genai · llm coding interview · ai engineer coding round · machine learning coding interview questions · genai take home assignment def reciprocal_rank_fusion(*ranked_lists: list[str], k: int = 60) -&gt; list[str]: &quot;&quot;&quot;Fuse ranked lists of ids; 1/(k+rank) per list, summed. A common coding-round question.&quot;&quot;&quot; scores: dict[str, float] = {} for ranked in ranked_lists: for rank, doc_id in enumerate(ranked, start=1): scores[doc_id] = scores.get(doc_id, 0.0) + 1.0 / (k + rank) return sorted(scores, key=scores.get, reverse=True) How should freshers prepare for a GenAI interview? Build one RAG project and one fine-tune before the interview, so every answer has a story. Read four papers: transformer, RAG, LoRA, QLoRA. Write the evaluation set for your project, because the evaluation question is where freshers lose. Rehearse the project walkthrough with a timer, failure by failure. Prepare three questions to ask about how the team evaluates and ships. Then be honest about what you have not done; the sentence "I have not done that, here is how I would start" gets hired. Also asked as: genai interview preparation for freshers · how to prepare for ai engineer interview · llm interview preparation · generative ai interview questions for freshers · ai interview tips · what to study for genai interview · genai interview roadmap 6topic areas every GenAIinterview covers4papers to read before any ofthem1project to know failure byfailure20labelled questions in theevaluation set that wins theKey numbers Questions to ask the interviewer How do you evaluate model changes before they ship? What does your logging show for a bad answer? How often do requirements change and how do you handle it? Who owns prompt versions? What was the last production incident and what changed after? These tell you whether the team treats LLM systems as engineering, and they tell the interviewer you do. # Hackathon judging criteria and a rubric organisers can copy: how judges score, how to brief a panel, how to break ties, and how to judge fairly in 15 minutes per team
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/hackathon-judging-criteria-and-rubric/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

What are the judging criteria for a hackathon? Four things, whatever the rubric calls them: feasibility, does it work and could it exist; innovation, is there a real insight, not a new coat of paint; practicality, would the stated user actually adopt it; and problem solving, did the team understand the problem before building. Presentation and teamwork are usually smaller weights. Organisers dress these up with different names; judges who have sat on panels recognise the same four underneath. Also asked as: hackathon judging criteria · hackathon evaluation criteria · hackathon rubric · hackathon judging rubric · how are hackathons judged · hackathon scoring criteria · hackathon judging parameters · what do hackathon judges look for · criteria for judging hackathon projects · hackathon marking scheme These four are the ones I put on the screen when I brief a judging room, because I learned them from the other side: three first prizes, one loss, and then panels of my own [1][2]. The full rubric with score anchors is on the portfolio and free to copy. Judges do not score the idea. They score the evidence: what ran, what the team understood, what they cut. Write the rubric so it can only be filled in from evidence. Pranjul Rathour A rubric you can copy Five criteria, weights that sum to one hundred, and score anchors at 2, 5 and 8 out of 10 so every judge means the same thing by a 7. Also asked as: hackathon rubric template · hackathon judging sheet · hackathon score sheet · hackathon evaluation sheet · hackathon judging template excel · hackathon rubric pdf · sample hackathon rubric · hackathon judging form The rubric, with anchorsCriterion (weight)Score 2Score 5Score 8Feasibility (25)Demo did not run or wasa video of a mock-upCore flow ran on seededdata with minor breaksFull flow ran live,architecture is honestand could deployProblem solving (25)Problem restated fromthe brief, no userevidenceProblem understood, oneuser assumption statedSpoke to or observedusers, constraintsnamed and honouredPracticality (20)No clear user oradoption pathPlausible user, unclearnext stepNamed user, realisticpilot, cost consideredInnovation (20)Existing tool renamedOne meaningfulimprovement on theexisting approachA sharp insight othersmissed, stated in onesentencePresentation (10)Read from slides, overtime, no demoClear story, demoshown, roughly on timeStory, demo, ask, inthree minutes, handledQ&amp;A wellThe rubric, with anchors Weights are a choice; my reasoning for putting feasibility and problem solving above innovation is that innovation is the easiest criterion to fake with words and the hardest to verify in three minutes [4]. For an AI hackathon, add one line under feasibility: is the model doing real work on real inputs, or is the AI a label on a rules engine? How should a judge spend the time per team? Fifteen minutes: three for the pitch, two for the demo if it was not live, five for questions, two to score alone, three to confer if the panel scores together. Judge the demo and the answers, not the deck. Ask at least one question that tests understanding rather than the project. Score independently before discussing, then discuss only where scores differ by more than two points. Also asked as: how to judge a hackathon · hackathon judging process · hackathon judging time per team · how to be a good hackathon judge · hackathon judge tips · hackathon judging best practices · judging a hackathon for the first time Fifteen minutes per team1Read the one-pagesummary before theywalk in2Three minutes ofpitch, uninterrupted3Demo, live orrecorded, with theteam narrating4Five minutes ofquestions, hardestfirst5Two minutes of silent,independent scoring6Three minutes toconfer where scoresdiffer by more thantwo7Write one line offeedback the team canact onFifteen minutes per team What questions should judges ask? Who is this for, and have you spoken to them? What happens when it fails? What did you build yourselves versus take from a library? Why did you cut what you cut? What would you do with a month? How is this different from the existing solution? What did you learn that surprised you? The first and last reveal problem understanding; the middle ones reveal feasibility and judgement. Also asked as: hackathon judge questions · questions judges ask at hackathons · hackathon q&amp;a questions · what to ask hackathon teams · hackathon jury questions · hackathon interview questions from judges Questions that separate teamsWho exactly is the user, and what did they tell you?Show me what happens with a bad inputWhich part was hardest, and how did you solve it?What is borrowed, what is yours?What did you cut and why?What breaks first if a hundred people use this tomorrow?What would change with a month?Questions that separate teams How do I brief a judging panel? Fifteen minutes before the first pitch, all judges in one room. Cover: the four criteria and their weights, the score anchors with one example each, the time protocol and who keeps time, the rule of independent scoring before discussion, conflicts of interest and how to declare them, tie-breaking, and how feedback is delivered. Hand each judge a one-page sheet per team. Ask them to score the demo they saw, not the potential they imagine. Also asked as: how to brief hackathon judges · judges briefing hackathon · hackathon judge orientation · what to tell hackathon judges · judge training hackathon · hackathon judge onboarding My briefing outline, which takes exactly fifteen minutes, is written up separately [3]. The two things new judges most need to hear: score independently first, and a working small thing beats a described big thing. Walking a room through evaluation criteria How do you break ties and handle conflicts of interest? Decide both before the event and write them down. Tie-break by a pre-declared criterion, usually feasibility, then problem solving, then a short re-demo if still tied; never by adding a new criterion in the room. Conflicts: any judge who has mentored a team, knows a member personally, or works for a sponsor whose product the team used declares it and abstains from scoring that team; the remaining judges' scores are normalised. Publish both rules to teams with the criteria. Also asked as: hackathon tie breaker · how to break ties in hackathon judging · hackathon judge conflict of interest · fair hackathon judging · hackathon judging bias · hackathon judging fairness · hackathon judging controversy Both processes, with the edge cases I have met, are written up in detail [5][6]. The commonest conflict at college hackathons is a mentor judging their own mentees, and the fix is simply to separate the two roles before the event. How should judges give feedback? One specific, actionable sentence per team, delivered privately or in writing, that names what would have moved the score: "the demo depended on Wi-Fi; seed the data next time", "you never named the user; start there". Not a ranking, not a critique of the idea, not encouragement without content. Teams remember one clear sentence for years, and it is the only part of judging that improves the next hackathon. Also asked as: hackathon judge feedback · how to give feedback to hackathon teams · hackathon feedback examples · constructive feedback hackathon · hackathon feedback form · post hackathon feedback My notes on feedback that actually helped teams, and the kind that did not, are on the portfolio [7]. How do the criteria differ for Smart India Hackathon or corporate hackathons? The four criteria hold; the weights and a fifth item shift. Smart India Hackathon panels include the problem statement's owners, so fit with existing systems and policy carries extra weight, and the current year's official rubric governs [10]. Corporate hackathons weight practicality toward the sponsor's platform or data. Community events such as those run under Major League Hacking publish organiser guidance that leans toward learning and inclusion [9]. Read the event's own rubric, then map it onto the four. Also asked as: smart india hackathon judging criteria · sih evaluation parameters · corporate hackathon judging criteria · mlh judging criteria · online hackathon judging criteria · ai hackathon judging criteria · hackathon judging criteria for students How weights shift by eventEvent typeWhat risesWhat to watchCampus hackathonFeasibility, learningJudges mentoring their ownteamsSmart India HackathonFit with the department&#x27;ssystems, constraints honouredDomain experts weightingpracticality heavilyCorporate sponsoredUse of the sponsor&#x27;s platform,practicalityTeams that used the platformsuperficially for pointsAI-themedWhether the model does realwork on real inputsRules engines labelled as AIOnlineRecorded demo quality,documentationVerifying the demo is realHow weights shift by event How do I become a hackathon judge? Build and ship something first, then attend, then mentor, then ask the organiser for a panel seat. Organisers want judges who have shipped, can follow a rubric, show up on time and write feedback. # Hackathon pitch deck template: the seven slides, the three-minute script, demo rules and what judges score, from three first prizes and the judging table
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/hackathon-pitch-deck-template/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

What should a hackathon pitch deck contain? Seven slides in this order: the problem in the user's words; the user and what the problem costs them; the live demo, which is not a slide but a switch to your app; how it works, one diagram; what you cut and why; what is next and what you need; the team with roles and contact details. Three minutes total, with about ninety seconds on the demo. Anything else, a market size, a competitor grid, a technology logo wall, comes out. Also asked as: hackathon pitch deck template · hackathon presentation template · hackathon ppt template · hackathon ppt format · hackathon presentation format · hackathon slides · how to make hackathon presentation · hackathon pitch deck example · hackathon ppt ideas · presentation for hackathon I have pitched from the floor three times for a first prize and once for a loss I still learn from, and I have sat on the other side scoring decks with a timer running [7][8]. The structure below is what wins from both seats. The downloadable version and the reasoning behind each slide are on the portfolio [1]. The judges have seen twenty decks today. They will remember one demo and one sentence. Build the deck to deliver exactly those two things. Pranjul Rathour What goes on each slide? One idea per slide, readable from the back of the room, with the words you will say, not paragraphs you will read. Here is each slide with its job and its time. Also asked as: hackathon slide content · what to include in hackathon ppt · hackathon problem statement slide · hackathon solution slide · hackathon architecture slide · hackathon team slide · how many slides for hackathon presentation The seven slidesSlideWhat is on itTime1 ProblemOne sentence in the user&#x27;swords, one number if you haveone20 seconds2 UserWho exactly, what they dotoday, what it costs them20 seconds3 DemoSwitch to the appthe happy path, seeded data,one flow end to end90 seconds4 How it worksOne diagram, four to sixboxes, the hardest parthighlighted20 seconds5 What we cutTwo features you dropped andthe reason, in one line each10 seconds6 Next and askThe next milestone and whatyou need, mentorship, a pilot,credits15 seconds7 TeamNames, roles, one contact, arepository link5 secondsThe seven slides The "what we cut" slide surprises teams, and it is the slide that has most often earned a nod from judges I have sat beside. It says: we understood the problem well enough to know what was not the problem. How do I structure a three-minute hackathon pitch? Thirty seconds of setup, ninety of demo, sixty of close. Setup: the user, the pain, and the one-line solution. Demo: the happy path, narrated in the user's terms, "Priya uploads her invoice, and here is the total, validated". Close: how it works, what you cut, what is next, the ask. Rehearse with a timer three times. If you run over in rehearsal, cut the setup, never the demo. Also asked as: 3 minute hackathon pitch · how to pitch in a hackathon · hackathon pitch structure · hackathon pitch script · how to present hackathon project in 3 minutes · hackathon presentation tips · how to give a hackathon presentation · elevator pitch hackathon The three minutes, second by second10:00 to 0:10: the userand the pain, onesentence20:10 to 0:30: whatexists today and whyit fails them, thenyour one-line solution30:30 to 2:00: livedemo of one completeflow, narrated as theuser42:00 to 2:20: how itworks, one diagram52:20 to 2:35: what youcut and why62:35 to 2:55: what isnext and the ask72:55 to 3:00: names,roles, contactThe three minutes, second by second What is a good opening line for a hackathon pitch? The user's name and their problem, in ten words. "Ramesh grows wheat near Kanpur and cannot read the advisory SMS." Not "Hi, we are Team Innovators and we built an AI-powered platform." The first sentence decides whether the judge listens to the second. My two-minute pitch notes cover the opening in detail [2][5]. Also asked as: hackathon pitch opening line · how to start a hackathon presentation · hackathon introduction speech · how to introduce your team in hackathon · hackathon pitch hook How do I demo without it crashing? Freeze the code two hours before. Seed the data so no step depends on a live third-party call or the venue Wi-Fi. Rehearse the exact click path three times on the machine and browser you will present from. Record a full-path video and keep it open in a tab. Assign one person to drive and one to talk. If it breaks anyway, switch to the video without apology and keep narrating; judges score recovery too. Also asked as: hackathon demo tips · how to demo at a hackathon · hackathon live demo · hackathon demo video · demo fails hackathon · how to present a working prototype · hackathon demo checklist Demo checklist, two hours beforeCode frozen, no new featuresSeeded data covers every step of the happy pathNo live network calls the demo depends on, or a mocked fallbackRehearsed three times on the presenting laptop and browserBackup video recorded and open in a tabFont size increased so the back row can readNotifications off, other tabs closed, charger connectedDriver and speaker roles fixedDemo checklist, two hours before Our loss at STROT came from a live API call over venue Wi-Fi [8]. My technical checklist for demos that survive is written up separately [3], and every team I mentor gets it before the event. Pitching at CSJMU, Kanpur What do judges score, and how does the deck serve it? Four things: feasibility, innovation, practicality and problem solving, with presentation as a smaller weight. The demo proves feasibility. The problem and user slides prove problem solving and practicality. The how-it-works slide and the "what we cut" slide show innovation and judgement. The close shows you know what a next step is. If a slide does not serve one of those four, remove it. Also asked as: what judges look for in hackathon presentation · hackathon judging criteria presentation · how to impress hackathon judges · hackathon evaluation criteria · how are hackathon pitches scored · hackathon rubric presentation Criterion to slide mappingCriterionWhere it is provenFeasibilityThe live demo and the architecture diagramProblem solvingThe problem and user slides, in the user&#x27;swordsPracticalityThe user slide, the demo&#x27;s realism, the pilotin the next-step slideInnovationThe one insight in how-it-works, and what youcutPresentationTiming, clarity, one idea per slide, recoveryunder failureCriterion to slide mapping How do I handle Q&amp;A after the pitch? Repeat the question aloud, answer the fair part in two sentences, and stop. Expect: who is this for and have you spoken to them; what happens when it fails; how is this different from the existing tool; what did you build versus borrow; what would you do with a month. Say "we did not get to that" when true. Judges test whether you understand your own project, and a short honest answer beats a long confident one every time. Inside it, keep the same order: the department's problem in its vocabulary, the demo or a video of it, one diagram, feasibility and the constraints you honoured, impact for the department and the citizen, and a pilot plan. Replace "the ask" with "how this runs inside the department next month". Ministry judges reward fit with existing systems more than novelty. Also asked as: sih ppt template · smart india hackathon ppt format · sih presentation template · sih idea presentation ppt · how to make sih ppt · sih pitch · smart india hackathon presentation tips What mistakes lose pitches? Opening with the team and the stack. A slide of technology logos. Reading paragraphs off the screen. Explaining the architecture before showing the product. A demo that depends on Wi-Fi. Running over time so the demo gets cut. Ending with "thank you" instead of an ask. Five people speaking in turn with no handoff. Every one of these is on the checklists above, and every one I have watched sink a good build. Also asked as: hackathon presentation mistakes · why hackathon pitches fail · hackathon pitch mistakes · common hackathon presentation errors · bad hackathon pitch What separates pitches in a judging roomLEVEL 1Readslides read aloud, nodemo, over timeLEVEL 2Showna demo happened, thestory was unclearLEVEL 3Tolduser first, demo in themiddle, one diagramLEVEL 4Judgedscope named, cutsexplained, a real nextstepLEVEL 5Wonall of that, in underthree minutes, with oneline the judges repeat atlunchWhat separates pitches in a judging room Do I need a video, a one-pager or a repository too? Yes to all three, and they take an hour. A two-minute screen recording of the demo for organisers and for your LinkedIn post. A one-page PDF with the problem, the solution, the diagram and the team, for judges who want to remember you. # Hackathon project ideas that win: 40 AI and software ideas for students, with the hard part of each, from three first prizes
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/hackathon-project-ideas/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

What makes a hackathon project idea good? A good hackathon idea has four properties: a named user with a real friction, a before-and-after a judge can see in one demo, a hard technical part your team can finish in the time available, and a plausible next step after the event. Ambition is not one of the four. Every first prize I have won came from a smaller idea than the teams we beat, executed completely. Also asked as: hackathon project ideas · hackathon ideas · best hackathon project ideas · best hackathon ideas · good hackathon ideas · unique hackathon ideas · cool hackathon ideas · hackathon ideas for beginners · hackathon ideas for students · how to find hackathon ideas · winning hackathon ideas KrishGyan won Changethon at IIT Roorkee because the demo was a farmer's voice note going in and spoken advice coming out, in the farmer's language, on WhatsApp, with no reading required [1]. Annapurna won BYTEBATTLE because a judge could watch one meal move from a hotel kitchen to a shelter through four clear roles [2]. BrandHive won Product Genesis because we showed the whole loop for a small business, not a features slide [3]. None of those ideas was novel. All of them were complete. Judges do not remember the idea. They remember the moment the demo worked and they understood who it was for. Pranjul Rathour How do I generate hackathon ideas fast? Use a three-column frame: an audience, a friction, and what technology removes it. Audiences: farmers, first-year students, small shopkeepers, clinic staff, college offices, delivery workers, parents. Frictions: a form, a queue, a language barrier, a lost document, a phone call nobody answers, a spreadsheet updated by hand. Technology: voice in and out, document extraction, a RAG assistant over one set of documents, a vision check, an agent that finishes one repetitive task. Combine any row from each column and you have a candidate in thirty seconds. Also asked as: how to come up with hackathon ideas · hackathon idea generator · how to brainstorm hackathon ideas · hackathon problem statement ideas · how to choose hackathon project · hackathon idea selection From frame to committed idea in two hours1List five audiencesyour team can actuallyreach this week2For each, name thesingle most annoyingfriction3Pick the threecombinations with theclearest before-and-after4Sketch the three-minute demo for eachon paper5Name the hardtechnical part and whoon the team can do it6Choose the one wherethe hard part fits ina day7Cut every feature noton the demo pathFrom frame to committed idea in two hours 40 hackathon project ideas, with the hard part named Each idea below states the user, the demo and the hard part. Change the audience to match your problem statement; the shape carries over. Also asked as: ai hackathon project ideas · ai project ideas for hackathon · machine learning hackathon ideas · generative ai hackathon ideas · llm hackathon ideas · web development hackathon ideas · app ideas for hackathon · hackathon ideas 2026 · social good hackathon ideas · fintech hackathon ideas · healthcare hackathon ideas · education hackathon ideas · agriculture hackathon ideas AI and generative AI Voice-first advisory over WhatsApp for farmers or shopkeepers: voice note in, spoken answer out, in a regional language. Hard part: speech recognition quality on real audio. KrishGyan is this idea [1]. RAG assistant over one college's documents, syllabus, notices, previous-year papers, with page citations. Hard part: chunking messy PDFs so retrieval works. Invoice or receipt extraction to a spreadsheet with validation that totals add up. Hard part: deterministic validation after the model extracts. Prescription reader that turns a photo into a medication schedule with reminders. Hard part: handwriting and drug-name normalisation; keep a human confirm step. Lecture recording to notes: transcribe, segment by topic, produce a summary and a quiz. Hard part: speaker diarisation and long-audio chunking. Resume to job-fit report for a specific posting, with the gaps and one project suggestion per gap. Hard part: avoiding generic output; ground it in the posting text. Government scheme eligibility checker by conversation: answer five questions, get the schemes you qualify for with the documents needed. Hard part: keeping the rules table accurate and cited. Code review agent for student repositories that comments on a pull request with tests it ran. Hard part: sandboxing and a tight tool set. Local-language news summariser for one district, from public feeds, with source links. Hard part: dedup across sources and honest attribution. Meeting-minutes agent that joins a call recording, extracts decisions and owners, and files them. Hard part: precision on who owns what. Agriculture and rural Crop disease photo triage with a confidence threshold and a "see an expert" path. Hard part: a model that admits uncertainty on out-of-distribution photos. Education and campus Attendance by face recognition with liveness, embeddings-only storage, per-class galleries. Hard part: threshold tuning and privacy design. Doubt-solving queue for a class, with an LLM first pass and a teacher escalation. Hard part: knowing when the model should not answer. Placement tracker that scrapes the college's notices and turns them into a calendar with deadlines. Hard part: parsing inconsistent notice formats. Lab equipment booking with conflict detection and a waitlist. Hard part: none technical, which is why it ships. Peer tutoring marketplace inside one campus, with verified student profiles. Hard part: trust and moderation. Exam paper generator from a syllabus with difficulty tags and an answer key, reviewed by a teacher. Hard part: quality control and avoiding hallucinated facts. Accessibility reader for scanned course PDFs: OCR to clean text to audio. Hard part: reading order on two-column pages. Health and public services Clinic queue and token system with SMS updates for a primary health centre. Hard part: works on feature phones. Vaccination or check-up reminders for a ward, by voice call in the local language. Hard part: opt-in, consent and unsubscribe from the first version. Blood donor coordination with availability and distance, verified by a hospital contact. Hard part: verification without friction. Medical report explainer: upload a lab report, get plain-language explanations of each line with the normal range cited, and a clear "ask your doctor" boundary. Hard part: restraint. Emergency contact card by QR for two-wheeler riders. Hard part: none; the demo is the product. Fintech and small business GST invoice generator for a kirana shop that works offline and syncs later. Hard part: none; polish wins. Loan document checklist assistant that tells a first-time applicant what is missing from their file. Hard part: accurate, cited requirements. Small-business review responder that drafts replies to Google reviews in the owner's voice, with approval before posting. Hard part: never auto-post. Civic, community and sustainability Surplus food coordination between donors, NGOs and volunteers with verified impact. Hard part: roles and trust; this is Annapurna [2][7]. Pothole and streetlight reporting with photo, location and a public status board. Hard part: dedup of the same issue reported twice. Lost-and-found for a campus or a city event with image matching. Hard part: cold start; seed it with the event's registrations. Prompt library with version stamps per model and date, so a team knows which prompt worked where. Hard part: the discipline; I run one at tools.scult.in. Which ideas suit an AI hackathon specifically? The ones where the model does one narrow job with real inputs and a visible output: voice in and voice out, a photo to a structured record, a document set to cited answers, a repository to a review with evidence. Ideas 1 to 10 above are built for that. Avoid "a chatbot for X" unless X is a specific document set and the demo shows a citation; judges have seen a thousand generic chatbots. Presenting KrishGyan, farming advice in your voice and language How do I adapt an idea to a Smart India Hackathon problem statement? Read the problem statement for its owner and its constraint. Each can be finished, polished and demoed by a team learning as they go, and a finished beginner project beats an unfinished ambitious one on every rubric I have used. Anything that needs a dataset you do not have on day one. Anything whose demo depends on a third party approving an API key during the event. # How does face recognition work? Detection, embeddings, thresholds and liveness, from building FaceVision
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/how-does-face-recognition-work/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

How does face recognition work? Face recognition works in four steps. A detector finds each face in the image and its landmarks. The face is aligned and cropped to a standard size. A recognition network turns the crop into an embedding, a vector of a few hundred numbers in which faces of the same person land close together. Finally the system compares that embedding with stored ones and declares a match when the distance falls under a threshold. Everything else, liveness, enrolment, privacy, is engineering around those four steps. Also asked as: how does face recognition work · how face recognition works · how facial recognition works · face recognition explained · what is face recognition · face recognition technology · how does facial recognition technology work · how face recognition works step by step The embedding idea comes from FaceNet, which trained a network so that the Euclidean distance between two face vectors directly measured how likely they were the same person [1]. ArcFace sharpened it with an angular margin loss that spreads identities further apart, and it is the recipe behind most open models today [2]. I built FaceVision in 2026 as a browser-only detection, recognition and liveness system: the camera frames never leave the device, only embeddings are sent to a FastAPI and PostgreSQL backend, and no image is ever stored [13]. This page is what that build taught me, with the papers underneath each step. The moment you decide never to store a face image, half your privacy problems disappear and the other half become simple. Store the vector, throw away the pixels. Pranjul Rathour, from building FaceVision What is the difference between face detection and face recognition? Face detection finds faces: it returns bounding boxes and usually landmarks for eyes, nose and mouth, for every face in a frame, and it does not know or care who they are. Face recognition takes one detected face and identifies or verifies the person. Detection is the first stage of recognition, but a security camera that counts people, or a phone that focuses on a face, needs only detection. Also asked as: what is face detection · face detection vs face recognition · difference between face detection and face recognition · face detection explained · face recognition vs facial recognition · what is facial recognition Detection, recognition, verification, identificationDetectionVerification (1:1)Identification (1:N)Question answeredWhere are the facesIs this person who they claimto beWho among N enrolled people isthisInputOne imageOne face plus one claimedidentityOne face plus a galleryOutputBoxes and landmarksYes or no with a scoreThe closest identity or noneTypical useCamera focus, counting,croppingPhone unlock, KYC, attendancecheck-inFinding a face in a databaseRiskLowMedium, one comparisonHighest, N comparisons raisefalse matchesDetection, recognition, verification, identification MTCNN was the standard detector for years [3]; RetinaFace improved accuracy on small and turned faces and remains a strong default [4]. Google's MediaPipe ships a fast detector that runs on phones and in browsers [11]. What is a face embedding, and how are faces compared? A face embedding is a fixed-length vector, often 128 or 512 numbers, produced by a network trained so that the same person's faces cluster together and different people's faces sit apart. Comparison is a distance: cosine similarity or Euclidean distance between two vectors. If the distance is below a threshold, the system calls it a match. The threshold is not part of the model; it is a decision you make from your own error data. Also asked as: what is face embedding · face recognition embeddings explained · how are faces compared · face similarity score · cosine similarity face recognition · face recognition threshold · face matching algorithm From camera frame to match decision1Detect faces and fivelandmarks2Align by rotating andscaling to thelandmark template3Crop to the model&#x27;sinput size, often 112by 1124Run the recognitionnetwork to get theembedding5Normalise the vectorto unit length6Compare with storedembeddings by cosineor Euclidean distance7Accept if under thethreshold, else rejector ask againFrom camera frame to match decision The embedding is why you never need to store the face image. A vector cannot be turned back into a photograph in any useful way, it is far smaller, and it can be compared in a database index like any other vector. FaceVision stores exactly this: the vector, the user id, the timestamp, nothing visual [13]. How do I choose the match threshold? Collect pairs of embeddings from your real users and cameras, labelled same-person or different-person, then plot the two error rates as the threshold moves: false accepts, a stranger let in, and false rejects, the right person turned away. Choose the threshold that meets your risk. A door lock wants false accepts near zero and tolerates retries; a class attendance system tolerates a few false accepts and hates queues. Never ship a vendor's default threshold blind. Also asked as: face recognition threshold · false accept rate vs false reject rate · how accurate is face recognition · face recognition accuracy · far vs frr · equal error rate face recognition · how to improve face recognition accuracy The two errors you are tradingFalse acceptFalse rejectWhat happensA different person is matchedThe genuine person is rejectedLower it byRaising the bar, a stricter thresholdLowering the bar, a looser thresholdCostsSecurity breach, wrong record, fraudFrustration, queues, support ticketsWho worriesSecurity and complianceUsers and operationsDial forPayments, access control, KYCAttendance, photo tagging, conveniencefeaturesThe two errors you are trading NIST's ongoing Face Recognition Technology Evaluation publishes false match and false non-match rates for hundreds of algorithms under controlled conditions, and it is the reference for what state-of-the-art accuracy looks like [5]. It also shows how far the same algorithm's numbers move between a mugshot-quality image and a webcam frame, which is why your own data matters more than the leaderboard. Why does face recognition fail? For a short list of reasons that repeat everywhere: low light and backlight, motion blur, extreme pose, masks and sunglasses, low-resolution or heavily compressed cameras, faces too small in the frame, enrolment photos that look nothing like daily conditions, and a threshold tuned on a different population. Twins and close relatives are a real limit for some models. Most "the AI is broken" tickets are a camera or lighting problem. Also asked as: why face recognition not working · face recognition not working · why does face recognition fail · face recognition problems · limitations of face recognition · can face recognition be fooled · can face recognition identify twins · can face recognition distinguish twins · face recognition in low light Debugging a face recognition failure, in orderIs the face detected at all? Check the detector&#x27;s boxes firstIs the face large enough? Aim for more than 80 pixels between the eyesIs the lighting on the face, not behind it?Is the pose within the model&#x27;s range, roughly 30 degrees of frontal?Does the enrolment embedding come from a similar camera and lighting?Is the threshold set from your own error curve?Are you comparing embeddings from the same model version?Debugging a face recognition failure, in order On twins: FaceVision, like every embedding system I have tested, sometimes cannot separate identical twins at a threshold that still rejects strangers. For high-stakes use, that is a reason to add a second factor, not a reason to loosen the threshold. Is face recognition biased, and how accurate is it across groups? Accuracy differs across demographic groups for most algorithms. NIST's 2019 demographic study measured higher false positive rates for some groups than others, with the size of the gap depending strongly on the algorithm [6]. The gap has narrowed in recent evaluations but has not vanished. The practical response is to test on your own user population, report the error rates per group, and choose a threshold and a fallback that protect the worst-served group, not the average. Also asked as: is face recognition biased · face recognition bias · facial recognition accuracy by race · face recognition demographic bias · is facial recognition accurate · face recognition fairness For a college attendance system in Kanpur, the relevant test set is your own students under your own classroom lights, not a benchmark shot in a studio elsewhere. What is liveness detection, and why do I need it? Liveness detection, also called presentation attack detection, checks that the face in front of the camera is a live person and not a printed photo, a phone screen showing a photo or video, or a mask. Without it, any recognition system that unlocks or pays can be defeated by a picture from social media. Active liveness asks the user to do something, blink, turn, follow a dot. Passive liveness analyses a single frame or short clip for texture, depth cues and screen artefacts. Also asked as: what is liveness detection · liveness detection face recognition · active vs passive liveness detection · how does liveness detection work · anti spoofing face recognition · can face recognition be fooled by photo · face liveness check · presentation attack detection Active versus passive livenessActivePassiveHow it worksUser performs a challenge, blink, turn, smileModel inspects the frame for print, screen andmask artefactsUser effortA few seconds, needs instructionsNone, invisibleSpoof resistanceGood against photos, weaker against videoreplayGood against photos and screens, depends onmodel qualityAccessibilityHarder for some usersEasierBest forKYC and onboardingFrequent check-ins such as attendanceActive versus passive liveness ISO/IEC 30107 defines the framework and terminology for presentation attack detection and the metrics vendors quote [7]. Texture analysis, the observation that a re-photographed face carries colour and frequency artefacts a live face does not, is one of the classic passive approaches [8]. FaceVision uses a passive check on the device before any embedding is computed, so a photo held to the camera is rejected before it can even be compared [13]. Presenting KrishGyan, farming advice in your voice and language Can I run face recognition in the browser, without a server seeing the face? Yes. ONNX Runtime Web runs detection, recognition and liveness models in the browser using WebAssembly or WebGPU [10]. The camera frame stays on the device, the models produce an embedding locally, and only the embedding travels to your API for comparison and storage. It is slower than a GPU server for large galleries, but for verification and small identification sets it is fast enough, and it removes the biggest privacy and compliance burden: you never possess a face image. Also asked as: face recognition in browser · face recognition javascript · onnx runtime web face recognition · on device face recognition · face recognition without server · client side face recognition · what is onnx runtime · face recognition privacy The architecture of FaceVision, which is the concrete version of this answer: FaceVision&#x27;s browser-first pipeline1Camera frames capturedin the browser2Detector and livenessmodel run in ONNXRuntime Web3Aligned crop embeddedon device4Embedding, not image,posted to a FastAPIendpoint5PostgreSQL storesembeddings per userfor enrolment6Verification comparesvectors server-sideand returns a scoreFaceVision&#x27;s browser-first pipeline Models are exported to ONNX from PyTorch or taken from open toolkits such as InsightFace, which publishes ArcFace-family recognition models and RetinaFace detectors [9]. Quantising them shrinks download size and speeds inference on phones, at a small accuracy cost you should measure. How do I build a face recognition attendance system? Enrol each person with three to five embeddings taken under the real classroom conditions, on the same kind of camera. At check-in, detect, run liveness, embed and compare against the enrolled set for that class only, which keeps the gallery small and the false-match rate low. Log the score, not the image. Add a fallback for rejections, such as a one-time code, so a bad lighting day does not stop a class. Publish the privacy notice before the first day. Also asked as: face recognition attendance system · how to make face recognition attendance system · face recognition attendance system python · best face recognition attendance system · face recognition attendance system project · face attendance system in college · attendance system using face recognition Attendance is the most common student project in this space and the one most often built wrong: images saved to a folder, a global gallery of thousands, no liveness, a threshold copied from a tutorial. Built right, with per-class galleries, on-device liveness and embeddings-only storage, it is also a strong portfolio piece, because you can explain each decision. Is face recognition legal in India, and how do I handle privacy? Facial data is biometric personal data, and India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, sets the framework for processing personal data with notice, consent, purpose limitation and security obligations [12]. Rules and enforcement continue to develop, so treat this as the direction, not legal advice. The engineering answer is independent of jurisdiction: collect consent, tell people what is stored and for how long, store embeddings rather than images, delete on request, and restrict who can run a search. Also asked as: is face recognition legal in india · face recognition privacy · face recognition data protection · face recognition consent · facial recognition law india · face recognition gdpr · face recognition ethics Privacy by design for a face systemWritten notice before enrolment: purpose, retention, who can accessExplicit consent recorded with the enrolmentEmbeddings stored, images discarded on devicePer-purpose galleries, never one global databaseDeletion path that removes embeddings within daysAccess logs for every searchThreshold and error rates documented and reviewedSecond factor for high-stakes decisionsPrivacy by design for a face system I wrote a longer note on what changed in my own practice after FaceVision, and most of it is the list above [14]. Which library or model should I use for face recognition? For a Python prototype: InsightFace for detection and ArcFace-family recognition, or the face_recognition library for simplicity at lower accuracy [9]. For phones and browsers: MediaPipe for detection [11] and an ONNX-exported ArcFace model in ONNX Runtime Web for recognition [10]. For anything that unlocks or pays: add a liveness model and test it against printed photos and phone screens yourself before you believe its numbers. Also asked as: best face recognition model · best face recognition library python · best face detection model · face recognition python · opencv face recognition · deepface vs insightface · face recognition api · best face recognition algorithm · mediapipe face detection 512numbers in a typical ArcFaceembedding0face images stored byFaceVision3 to 5enrolment samples per personunder real conditions2factors for anything thatunlocks or paysKey numbers What are common face recognition interview questions? Explain detection versus recognition versus verification versus identification. Explain what an embedding is and why distance measures similarity. Explain how you would set a threshold and what false accept and false reject mean. Explain what liveness detection defends against. Explain how you would design the system so no face image is stored. If you can answer these from a project you built, you are ahead of most candidates. Also asked as: face recognition interview questions · computer vision interview questions face recognition · biometrics interview questions · face recognition project explanation From my carousel5 Production AI Apps, All Open Source · 8 slides · full deck on Instagram and LinkedIn Where should I start with a face recognition project? Build verification first, not identification: enrol yourself and two friends, run detection and embedding in the browser with ONNX Runtime Web, store only embeddings, and plot your own false accept and false reject curve from a hundred attempts. Then add passive liveness and try to fool it with a photo of yourself. That project teaches every concept on this page and is exactly the shape of FaceVision. Also asked as: face recognition project · face recognition project ideas · face recognition tutorial · learn face recognition · face recognition course · face recognition for beginners · how to start with computer vision If your college wants a hands-on session on computer vision that respects privacy from the first line of code, that is one of the talks I offer. # How does OCR work? From Tesseract to document AI: turning scanned PDFs and invoices into searchable, structured text
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/how-does-ocr-work/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

What is OCR and how does it work? OCR, optical character recognition, converts images of text, a scanned page, a photo of a receipt, a PDF that is really a picture, into machine-readable text. It works in three stages: detection finds where text is on the page, recognition reads the characters in each region, and layout analysis puts the pieces back in reading order with their structure, paragraphs, columns, tables. Modern systems do all three with neural networks; older ones like classic Tesseract use hand-built image processing for the first and third. Also asked as: what is ocr · what is ocr technology · how does ocr work · what is ocr in computer · what is ocr in pdf · ocr meaning · optical character recognition explained · how ocr works step by step · what is ocr scanning The distinction that saves the most time: a "PDF" may already contain text, in which case you do not need OCR at all, only extraction. Check with a PDF library first; PyMuPDF will tell you in one call whether a page has a text layer [11]. OCR is for pages that are only pixels. I built two document systems in 2026 that sit on top of OCR: DocuLens AI, which extracts and compliance-checks invoices and contracts with schema validation [13], and the OCR &amp; Speech Workspace, which OCRs large PDFs concurrently in page batches and turns each document into a searchable knowledge base with page-level citations [12]. This page is the pipeline underneath both. Nobody wants OCR. They want the total from the invoice, the clause from the contract, the answer from the manual, with the page number. OCR is the first ten percent of that. Pranjul Rathour, from building DocuLens AI What are the stages of an OCR pipeline? Preprocess the image: deskew, denoise, binarise, fix resolution. Detect text regions and their orientation. Recognise the characters in each region into strings with confidence scores. Reconstruct layout: reading order, columns, paragraphs, tables, headers and footers. Post-process: spell-check against a lexicon, normalise numbers and dates, attach page and position to every span. Then either store the text for search or pass it to an extraction step. Also asked as: ocr pipeline · ocr process steps · ocr preprocessing · text detection vs text recognition · ocr architecture · how to build an ocr system · ocr post processing · document layout analysis The OCR pipeline, page by page1Render or load thepage at 300 DPI2Preprocess: deskew,denoise, threshold3Detect text regionsand orientation4Recognise charactersin each region withconfidence5Reconstruct readingorder, columns andtables6Post-process: lexicon,number and datenormalisation7Store text with pageand bounding boxes forcitationsThe OCR pipeline, page by page Detection is where CRAFT-style networks replaced connected-component heuristics, finding text at odd angles and sizes [3]. Recognition moved from character classifiers to sequence models, and TrOCR showed a pure transformer encoder-decoder could read lines end to end with pre-trained vision and language models [4]. Layout is where the hardest problems remain, and where document-understanding models entered. What is Tesseract, and is it still good? Tesseract is the open-source OCR engine originally developed at HP and later at Google, now maintained as a community project [1]. Version 4 added an LSTM-based recogniser, which made it good on clean, printed, well-scanned text in dozens of languages, and it remains free, offline and scriptable, with OCRmyPDF wrapping it to add text layers to scanned PDFs [10]. It is still the right tool for clean printed pages at zero cost. It is the wrong tool for photos, handwriting, complex tables and forms. Also asked as: what is tesseract ocr · is tesseract still good · tesseract vs easyocr · tesseract vs paddleocr · best free ocr · open source ocr · tesseract accuracy · how to use tesseract ocr python · pytesseract Open-source OCR enginesTesseractPaddleOCREasyOCRStrengthMature, many languages,offline, OCRmyPDF integrationStrong detection andrecognition, tables,multilingual, activelySimple Python API, 80+languagesWeaknessWeak on photos, handwritingand complex layoutHeavier setupSlower, less accurate on hardlayoutsBest forClean scanned documents atzero costProduction pipelines that needlayout and tablesQuick prototypes and scriptsSource[1][8][9]Open-source OCR engines Smith's 2007 overview of the engine's architecture is still the best short explanation of how a classic OCR engine thinks about a page [2]. How do vision-language models change OCR? Vision-language models read the page image directly and output text, structure or answers, without a separate detection and recognition stage. They handle mixed layouts, tables, handwriting and low-quality scans far better than classic engines, they can output Markdown with headings and tables preserved, and they can be asked for specific fields in one step. The cost is that they run as API calls or on a GPU, they can hallucinate plausible text where the image is unreadable, and they need validation downstream. Also asked as: ocr with llm · vision language model ocr · llm for document extraction · gpt for ocr · ocr free document understanding · donut model · layoutlm · best ai ocr · ai ocr vs traditional ocr LayoutLM pre-trained on text plus its position on the page and set the pattern for document understanding [5]; Donut showed that a model could go straight from pixels to structured output with no OCR engine at all [6]. Mistral's document API is one of several commercial options that return page text as Markdown with tables and images preserved [7], and it is what the OCR &amp; Speech Workspace uses for its page batches [12]. Classic OCR versus vision-language OCRClassic engine (Tesseract)Vision-language modelClean printed pagesExcellent, freeExcellent, costs per pagePhotos, skew, low lightPoorGoodTables and formsWeak, needs separate logicGood, can output Markdown tablesHandwritingPoorFair to good depending on modelHallucination riskNone, it reads or failsReal, it may invent plausible textCostFree, CPUAPI pricing or a GPUOfflineYesOnly with an open model on your hardwareClassic OCR versus vision-language OCR The hallucination row is the one to remember. A classic engine produces garbage on a bad scan and you can see it is garbage. A language model produces a fluent, wrong invoice total. Validation is not optional. How do I OCR a PDF for free? If the PDF already has text, extract it with PyMuPDF or a similar library and skip OCR [11]. If it is a scan, run OCRmyPDF, which uses Tesseract to add an invisible text layer so the PDF becomes searchable and copyable [10]. For photos or messy pages, PaddleOCR or EasyOCR in a short Python script. For the best quality on hard documents at some cost, a vision-language document API. All of the open tools run offline on a laptop. Also asked as: how to ocr a pdf · how to ocr a pdf for free · how to make a scanned pdf searchable · ocr pdf python · free ocr software · best free ocr for pdf · convert scanned pdf to text · how to extract text from scanned pdf · ocr online free The check-then-OCR pattern in Python: import fitz # PyMuPDF doc = fitz.open(&quot;scan.pdf&quot;) for page in doc: text = page.get_text() if text.strip(): use(text, page.number + 1) # already has a text layer else: pix = page.get_pixmap(dpi=300) # render, then OCR this page only text = ocr_engine(pix.tobytes(&quot;png&quot;)) use(text, page.number + 1) Keep the page number with every span from the first line. Every citation, search result and audit trail later depends on it. How do I OCR large PDFs quickly? Split by page, process pages concurrently in batches sized to your engine's or API's rate limit, and merge in page order. A 500-page manual is 500 independent jobs; a concurrency of eight turns an hour into minutes. Cache results by document hash and page, so a re-upload does not re-OCR. Store text per page, not per document, so retrieval and citations stay page-precise. Also asked as: ocr large pdf · batch ocr pdf · ocr many pages fast · parallel ocr python · ocr performance · ocr at scale · how long does ocr take Page-batched concurrency is the design of the OCR &amp; Speech Workspace: pages fan out to the document API in batches, results land in a per-page store with the page number, and the document becomes a scoped knowledge base whose answers cite exact pages [12]. Requirements gathering and user flows, on stage How accurate is OCR, and how do I improve it? On clean 300 DPI scans of printed English, modern engines exceed 99 percent character accuracy. Accuracy falls with low resolution, skew, shadows, coloured backgrounds, unusual fonts, handwriting and dense tables, and it falls hardest on the characters that matter most in business documents: digits. Improve it by fixing the input first, resolution, deskew, contrast, then choosing the right engine for the page type, then validating with rules, and only then by trying a bigger model. Also asked as: ocr accuracy · how to improve ocr accuracy · why ocr is not accurate · ocr accuracy on handwriting · ocr for low quality images · ocr digits accuracy · ocr confidence score Fixing OCR quality, in the order that paysScan or render at 300 DPI, not 72Deskew and crop to the pageIncrease contrast, binarise if the engine wants itCheck the language pack or model matches the documentHandle rotation, detect and rotate before recognisingUse confidence scores to flag low-confidence spans for reviewValidate numbers, dates and IDs with rules after recognitionOnly then, try a stronger modelFixing OCR quality, in the order that pays What is document AI, and how is it different from OCR? Document AI is OCR followed by understanding: classifying the document type, locating the fields that matter, extracting them into a schema you defined, validating them, and returning confidence per field. OCR gives you a wall of text. Document AI gives you an invoice number, a vendor, line items and a total, typed and checked. The extraction may use a language model with a strict output schema, a layout model trained on forms, or both. Also asked as: what is document ai · document ai vs ocr · intelligent document processing · idp vs ocr · document understanding ai · document extraction ai · what is idp · ai document processing From pixels to trusted dataLEVEL 1Imagea scan or photo, nothingmachine-readableLEVEL 2TextOCR output with pagenumbers and positionsLEVEL 3Structureheadings, tables andreading order preservedLEVEL 4Fieldsthe values you need,extracted into a schemaLEVEL 5Validatedevery field checked byrules, with confidence,ready for a system ofrecordFrom pixels to trusted data DocuLens AI is the field-and-validation layer: extraction through a language model constrained to a JSON schema, then deterministic checks and a compliance score computed the same way every time, so finance and legal users can rely on it [13]. How do I extract invoice data I can trust? Define the schema first: the fields, their types, and the rules between them. Extract with a model constrained to that schema, or with a layout model trained on invoices. Then validate deterministically: line items must sum to the subtotal, tax must match the rate, dates must parse, the invoice number must match the vendor's pattern, currency must be stated. Flag anything that fails for a human. Score each document the same way every time. Never let the model be the last word on a number. Also asked as: invoice ocr · how to extract data from invoices · invoice extraction ai · invoice data extraction python · ocr for invoices · extract fields from invoice · invoice parsing llm · receipt ocr The validation rules that catch most extraction errorsRuleWhat it catchesLine items sum to subtotalMissed rows, misread digitsSubtotal plus tax equalstotalTax rate confusion, decimal slipsDates parse and are inorderDay-month swaps, OCR confusing 1 and 7Invoice number matchesvendor patternHallucinated identifiersCurrency stated andconsistentMixed currency on multi-page documentsRequired fields presentTruncated pages, missed regionsThe validation rules that catch most extraction errors Determinism matters because the same invoice must produce the same result on Tuesday as on Monday. That is why DocuLens computes scores from rules, not from a model's opinion [13]. Can OCR read handwriting? Partly. Handwriting recognition on clean, separated block letters works reasonably with modern models; cursive, mixed scripts and forms with lines through the text remain hard. Vision-language models do better than classic engines, and confidence scores plus human review are essential. For Indian forms, mixed Hindi and English handwriting on printed templates, the practical approach is to recognise the printed template's fields, then OCR each handwritten field region separately with the expected type as a constraint, and route low-confidence results to a person. Also asked as: can ocr read handwriting · handwriting ocr · handwriting recognition ai · ocr for handwritten forms · icr vs ocr · handwriting to text ai · ocr hindi handwriting Which OCR should I use: Tesseract, PaddleOCR, EasyOCR, or an API? Tesseract via OCRmyPDF for clean scanned documents at zero cost [1][10]. PaddleOCR when you need tables, multilingual pages and production quality on your own hardware [8]. EasyOCR for a quick script [9]. A vision-language document API when documents are messy, layouts matter and you can pay per page and validate the output [7]. Most real pipelines use two: a cheap engine first, an expensive model only on pages the cheap one fails. Also asked as: best ocr · best ocr api · best ocr for python · best ocr for invoices · best ocr for tables · best ocr 2026 · paddleocr vs tesseract vs easyocr · google vision ocr vs tesseract · azure ocr vs aws textract Is the document clean, printed and single-column?YESTesseract through OCRmyPDF. Free, offline, goodenough, done.NOPhotos, tables, forms or handwriting: a vision-language document model, page-batched, with rulevalidation after.Is the document clean, printed and single-column? 300DPI to render before OCR3stages in every OCR pipeline1page number attached toevery span, always2engines in most realpipelines, cheap first thenKey numbers What are common OCR and document AI interview questions? Explain the three stages and where errors come from. Compare classic OCR with vision-language models, including the hallucination risk. Describe how you would OCR a 1,000-page PDF quickly. Explain how you would validate an extracted invoice. Describe how page-level citations work in a document chatbot. If you have built one extraction pipeline with validation, you can answer all of them. Also asked as: ocr interview questions · document ai interview questions · computer vision interview questions ocr · idp interview questions From my carousel5 Production AI Apps, All Open Source · 8 slides · full deck on Instagram and LinkedIn Where should I start with an OCR project? Take twenty real documents you have, invoices, marksheets, notes, and build the check-then-OCR script above with Tesseract. Measure character accuracy on five pages by hand. Then swap in a vision-language model for the pages that fail and add three validation rules. You will have learned every concept on this page, and the pipeline will be the shape of a real product. My longer design note on the pipeline is on the portfolio [14]. For a hands-on document AI session at your college, email pranjulrathour41@gmail.com or use pranjulrathour.scult.in/invite.
