# How to fine-tune an LLM: LoRA, QLoRA, datasets and evaluation, from building a fine-tuning platform
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/how-to-fine-tune-an-llm/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

What is fine-tuning an LLM? Fine-tuning is continuing to train a pre-trained language model on your own examples so that its weights shift toward your task: your tone, your output format, your domain's vocabulary, or a narrow skill the base model does badly. You start from a model that already understands language and nudge it, which is why a few thousand good examples can change behaviour that no prompt could. Also asked as: what does fine tuning llm mean · what is fine tuning in ai · what is fine tuning in machine learning · fine tuning meaning · what is llm fine tuning · what is supervised fine tuning The base model learned from trillions of tokens of general text. Fine-tuning shows it a comparatively tiny, curated set of input and output pairs and adjusts the weights to make those outputs more likely. The result is a model that behaves differently by default, without a long prompt reminding it every time. I built FineTune Studio in 2026 to turn this into a product workflow: upload a dataset, pick a base model, set LoRA or QLoRA hyper-parameters, launch a run, and watch the loss stream to the browser in real time [15]. Most of what follows is what that platform taught me about which decisions matter. Fine-tuning is not how you teach a model facts. It is how you teach a model habits. If you remember one line from this page, make it that one. Pranjul Rathour, from building FineTune Studio How does fine-tuning an LLM work? Training runs the model on each example, compares its predicted next tokens with the target answer, computes a loss, and adjusts weights by gradient descent to lower that loss. Full fine-tuning updates every weight, which needs enormous memory. Parameter-efficient methods freeze the base model and train a small set of added weights instead, which is what almost everyone outside a large lab does today. Also asked as: how does fine tuning llm work · how fine tuning works in llm · fine tuning process llm · how to fine tuning llm · llm fine tuning explained A fine-tuning run, end to end1Define the behaviouryou want and write 20examples by hand2Build and validate thedataset in a chattemplate3Pick a base model thatfits your GPU4Configure LoRA orQLoRA: rank, alpha,learning rate, epochs5Train and watchtraining versusvalidation loss6Evaluate base versusfine-tuned on held-outprompts7Merge, quantise andserveA fine-tuning run, end to end Lialin et al. survey the parameter-efficient family, adapters, prompt tuning, LoRA and their relatives, and the trade-offs between them [3]. In practice the field has converged: LoRA when memory allows, QLoRA when it does not. When should I fine-tune instead of using RAG or prompting? Fine-tune when the problem is behaviour: consistent style, strict structured output, a domain's phrasing, a classification or extraction skill, or when you need a small model to do one thing well and cheaply. Use RAG when the problem is knowledge that changes or must be cited. Use prompting first in every case, because a prompt is free to change and a fine-tune is not. Also asked as: rag vs fine tuning · fine tuning vs prompt engineering · when to fine tune llm · fine tuning vs rag vs prompt engineering · should i fine tune an llm · fine tuning vs few shot Have you exhausted prompting and RAG?YESThe model still gets the style, format or skillwrong with good context. Fine-tune on examplesof the right output.NOFix the prompt, add retrieval, or add few-shotexamples first. It is faster, cheaper andreversible.Have you exhausted prompting and RAG? The order I insist on with clients: prompt, then retrieval, then few-shot examples in the prompt, then fine-tuning. Each step is more expensive and less reversible than the last. Teams that fine-tune first usually end up fine-tuning again a month later when the requirements move. Does fine-tuning add knowledge to a model? Only weakly and unreliably. Fine-tuning on facts can make a model repeat those facts, but it cannot cite them, it forgets them as the world changes, and it tends to blend them with what it already believed. If the answer must be correct and traceable, retrieve it. LIMA showed that a thousand carefully chosen examples were enough to teach strong instruction-following, and that the knowledge came almost entirely from pre-training [6]. That is the clearest evidence for "fine-tune for behaviour, retrieve for facts". Also asked as: can fine tuning add knowledge · does fine tuning teach new information · fine tuning for knowledge injection · fine tuning vs rag for knowledge What is LoRA? LoRA, low-rank adaptation, freezes the original model weights and trains two small matrices per targeted layer whose product approximates the weight update. Instead of updating billions of parameters you train a few million, the adapter, which is a few megabytes on disk and can be swapped or merged. Hu et al. introduced it in 2021 and showed quality comparable to full fine-tuning at a fraction of the memory [1]. Also asked as: what is lora in ai · what is lora fine tuning · lora meaning in machine learning · how does lora work · lora explained · what is lora adapter The word LoRA also names a long-range radio protocol, which is why half the search results for "what is LoRA" are about antennas. In machine learning it is always low-rank adaptation. Two settings define an adapter: Rank (r). The inner dimension of the two matrices. Higher rank means more capacity and more memory. Typical values run from 8 to 64; I start at 16. Alpha. A scaling factor applied to the adapter's output. A common rule is alpha equal to rank or twice the rank; what matters is the ratio, since it changes the effective learning rate of the adapter. What are the target modules? Target modules are the layers inside the transformer that get an adapter. Attention projections (query, key, value, output) are the classic choice; adding the feed-forward projections usually improves results at some memory cost. The QLoRA paper found applying adapters to all linear layers mattered more than rank for matching full fine-tuning [2]. Also asked as: lora target modules · which layers to apply lora · lora rank and alpha · lora hyperparameters What is QLoRA, and what is the difference between LoRA and QLoRA? QLoRA is LoRA on top of a base model quantised to 4 bits. The frozen weights are stored in a compact NormalFloat4 format and de-quantised on the fly during the forward pass, while the small adapters train in higher precision. Dettmers et al. showed a 65B model fine-tuning on a single 48 GB GPU with quality matching 16-bit full fine-tuning [2]. The difference from LoRA is memory: same adapters, much smaller base. Also asked as: what is qlora · what is lora and qlora · lora vs qlora · difference between lora and qlora · qlora explained · qlora vs full fine tuning LoRA versus QLoRA versus full fine-tuningLoRAQLoRAFull fine-tuningBase weightsFrozen, 16-bitFrozen, 4-bit quantisedAll trainedTrained parametersAdapters, well under 1%Adapters, well under 1%100%Memory for a 7B modelRoughly 16 to 20 GBRoughly 6 to 10 GBWell over 100 GB withoptimiser statesSpeedFastSlower per step due to de-quantisationSlowest and most expensiveQualityClose to full for most tasksClose to LoRAThe ceilingOutputSmall adapter fileSmall adapter fileA full new modelLoRA versus QLoRA versus full fine-tuning The memory figures are orders of magnitude, not promises; they move with sequence length, batch size and gradient checkpointing. The reason QLoRA matters to students is simple: it is the technique that puts a 7B model on a free Colab T4 or a 16 GB laptop GPU. FineTune Studio's whole premise is that fine-tuning is a browser workflow, not a cluster job, and QLoRA is why that premise holds [15]. What is quantisation, and what are GGUF, AWQ and GPTQ? Quantisation stores weights in fewer bits, 8 or 4 instead of 16, which shrinks memory and speeds inference at a small accuracy cost. GGUF is the file format used by llama.cpp for running quantised models on CPUs and consumer GPUs [13]; AWQ and GPTQ are post-training quantisation methods aimed at GPU inference. QLoRA's NormalFloat4 is a quantisation for training. Quantise after fine-tuning and merging, not before, unless you are doing QLoRA. Also asked as: what is quantization in llm · gguf vs awq vs gptq · how to quantize a fine tuned model · 4 bit quantization llm · what is gguf How do I prepare a dataset for fine-tuning? Write the behaviour you want as a spec, then collect or write examples that follow it exactly, in the chat format the base model expects: a system message, a user turn and the ideal assistant answer. Deduplicate, validate every row, hold out ten to twenty percent for evaluation, and read a random sample by eye before training. Consistency beats size; a thousand examples that all follow the spec outperform fifty thousand that mostly do. Also asked as: how to prepare dataset for fine tuning · fine tuning dataset format · best fine tuning datasets · how much data to fine tune llm · alpaca format vs sharegpt format · chat template fine tuning · how to create dataset for llm Dataset checklist before you press trainA one-paragraph spec of the behaviour you are teachingEvery example in the base model&#x27;s chat template, applied by the tokenizerSystem prompt identical across examples if you will use one in productionExact duplicates and near-duplicates removedHeld-out validation split that never touches trainingSequence lengths measured, outliers trimmed or splitLabels only on assistant turns, not on the user&#x27;s textRandom sample of 50 rows read by a humanDataset checklist before you press train Alpaca popularised the instruction, input, output format with 52,000 generated examples [8]; ShareGPT-style multi-turn conversations followed. Both are just JSON shapes. What the model actually sees is the rendered chat template, so use the tokenizer's template function rather than hand-writing the special tokens [11]. Mismatched templates are the most common reason a fine-tuned chat model produces garbage. How much data do I need to fine-tune an LLM? For style, tone and format, a few hundred high-quality examples produce a visible change. For a classification or extraction skill, a few thousand. For a new domain's language, tens of thousands. Below a hundred, prompting with examples usually does as well. LIMA's thousand examples are the reference point for how little alignment data can be if it is clean [6]. Also asked as: how much data to fine tune llm · minimum dataset size for fine tuning · how many examples for fine tuning gpt · fine tuning with small dataset Can I use synthetic data for fine-tuning? Yes, and most teams do, by having a stronger model generate examples from a spec or from seed documents. It works when you filter hard: validate every synthetic example against the spec, deduplicate, and mix in real examples so the model does not learn the generator's tics. Alpaca itself was trained on synthetic data generated from 175 human-written seeds [8]. Also asked as: synthetic data for fine tuning · how to generate training data with llm · is synthetic data good for fine tuning Which base model should I fine-tune? Pick the smallest open-weight model that already does the task acceptably with a prompt, in a size that fits your GPU with QLoRA, with a licence you can ship under. Start from the instruct variant when your task is conversational and from the base variant when you are teaching a completion format from scratch. Small models, 1 to 4 billion parameters, fine-tune faster, serve cheaper and are often enough. Also asked as: best llm to fine tune · best open source model for fine tuning · base model vs instruct model fine tuning · which model to fine tune for chatbot · small language models fine tuning · can gemma be fine tuned · fine tune llama vs mistral In my own write-up of a run on FineTune Studio, a 1.7-billion-parameter model fine-tuned with QLoRA in about 3.2 GB of VRAM [16]. That is laptop territory. The trade-off you accept is ceiling: a small model learns a narrow behaviour well and generalises less. For a support-ticket classifier that is exactly right. For an open-ended assistant it is not. Can I fine-tune GPT or other closed models? Yes, through the vendor's API. OpenAI offers fine-tuning of selected models with an upload-and-train workflow, priced per training and inference token [14]. You get no weights, no adapter file and no local inference; you get a model identifier. It is the right choice when you already depend on that vendor and do not want to run inference yourself, and the wrong one when you need control, portability or offline use. Also asked as: how to fine tune gpt · can i fine tune gpt 4 · how to fine tune gpt 4o · fine tune chatgpt on my data · openai fine tuning cost · how to fine tune claude How do I fine-tune an LLM on a free GPU or locally? Use QLoRA with a 1 to 7 billion parameter model, a sequence length trimmed to your data, gradient checkpointing, a small batch with gradient accumulation, and a library that handles the memory tricks: Hugging Face PEFT with TRL's SFTTrainer, or Unsloth for faster and leaner runs. A free Colab T4 with 16 GB handles a 7B QLoRA run at short sequence lengths; a 12 to 16 GB laptop GPU handles 1 to 4B comfortably. Also asked as: how to fine tune llm locally · fine tune llm on colab free · fine tune llm on consumer gpu · how much vram to fine tune llm · best gpu for fine tuning llm · fine tune llm on cpu · fine tune llm on mac VRAM budget for a QLoRA run, rough orders of magnitude1 to 2B model3 to 4B model7 to 8B model4-bit base weightsUnder 1.5 GBAbout 2 to 3 GBAbout 4 to 5 GBAdapters and optimiserHundreds of MBHundreds of MBAround 1 GBActivations at 1,024tokens, batch 11 to 2 GB with checkpointing2 to 3 GB3 to 5 GBFits comfortably onAny 6 GB GPU8 GB GPU16 GB GPU or free Colab T4VRAM budget for a QLoRA run, rough orders of magnitude The minimal PEFT and TRL recipe, trimmed to the lines that matter: from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, BitsAndBytesConfig from peft import LoraConfig from trl import SFTTrainer, SFTConfig bnb = BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type=&quot;nf4&quot;, bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=&quot;bfloat16&quot;) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(BASE, quantization_config=bnb, device_map=&quot;auto&quot;) tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(BASE) lora = LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, lora_dropout=0.05, task_type=&quot;CAUSAL_LM&quot;, target_modules=&quot;all-linear&quot;) cfg = SFTConfig(output_dir=&quot;out&quot;, num_train_epochs=2, learning_rate=2e-4, per_device_train_batch_size=2, gradient_accumulation_steps=8, gradient_checkpointing=True, max_length=1024, eval_strategy=&quot;steps&quot;, eval_steps=50, logging_steps=10) trainer = SFTTrainer(model=model, args=cfg, train_dataset=train, eval_dataset=val, processing_class=tok, peft_config=lora) trainer.train() Argument names shift between library versions, so check the current TRL and PEFT documentation rather than copying blindly [9][10]. Unsloth wraps the same idea with custom kernels that cut memory and time further [12]. Walking a room through the products he has shipped Which hyper-parameters matter for fine-tuning? Four: learning rate, number of epochs, LoRA rank with its alpha, and effective batch size. Learning rate too high and the loss spikes or the model forgets; too low and nothing changes. More than two or three epochs on a small dataset usually means memorising it. Rank 8 to 32 covers most tasks. Everything else, dropout, warm-up, scheduler, stays at library defaults until an experiment says otherwise. Also asked as: qlora hyperparameters · fine tuning hyperparameters llm · learning rate for lora · how many epochs to fine tune llm · lora rank 8 vs 16 vs 64 · batch size for fine tuning A defensible starting grid, which is what FineTune Studio pre-fills: learning rate 2e-4 for adapters, 2 epochs, rank 16 with alpha 32, effective batch size 16 through accumulation, warm-up of a few percent of steps. Change one variable per run, keep the eval set fixed, and write down what you changed. Fine-tuning without a lab notebook is guessing with a GPU bill. How do I read the loss curve? Watch two lines: training loss should fall steadily; validation loss should fall with it and then flatten. The moment validation loss turns upward while training loss keeps falling, the model is memorising the training set and you should stop at the earlier checkpoint. A training loss that never falls means the learning rate is too low, the data is inconsistent, or the template is wrong. A loss that collapses to near zero in the first steps means leaked labels or duplicated data. Also asked as: how to read loss curve fine tuning · training loss vs validation loss llm · what is a good loss for fine tuning · loss not decreasing fine tuning · overfitting in fine tuning · when to stop fine tuning What the loss curve is telling youLEVEL 1Flat from the startlearning rate too low,wrong template, or frozenlayers you meant to trainLEVEL 2Falling, validationtracks ithealthy run, keep goingLEVEL 3Validation flattensyou have learned what thedata can teach, stop hereLEVEL 4Validation rises,training fallsmemorising, roll back tothe best checkpointLEVEL 5Sudden spikeslearning rate too high ora bad batch, lower it andresumeWhat the loss curve is telling you Live telemetry is the feature I built FineTune Studio around: loss, learning rate and throughput stream to the browser over WebSockets so a run can be judged in the first few hundred steps rather than discovered as a waste hours later [15]. How do I evaluate a fine-tuned model honestly? Hold out prompts the model never trained on and compare the base model and the fine-tuned model on the same prompts side by side, scored against your spec by a rubric, by exact match where outputs are structured, and by a human for a sample. Report the comparison, not the fine-tuned model alone; a fine-tune that is not better than the base with a good prompt should not ship. Also test a few general prompts to catch forgetting. Also asked as: how to evaluate fine tuned model · fine tuning evaluation metrics · how to test a fine tuned llm · base vs fine tuned comparison · llm evaluation after fine tuning · perplexity fine tuning Perplexity on held-out text is cheap and tells you the model has learned the distribution; it does not tell you the outputs are useful. For structured outputs, parse them and measure exact-field accuracy. For free text, a rubric scored by a stronger model plus a human sample is the workable compromise. FineTune Studio shows base and fine-tuned answers to the same prompt next to each other for exactly this reason: the effect of a run should be visible before anything is deployed [15]. What is catastrophic forgetting? Catastrophic forgetting is when fine-tuning on a narrow task degrades the model's general abilities, because the weights that encoded them were overwritten. Luo et al. measured it across model sizes and found it increases with more aggressive training [7]. LoRA reduces it by touching fewer weights; lower learning rates, fewer epochs, and mixing a slice of general instruction data into your dataset reduce it further. Also asked as: catastrophic forgetting fine tuning · how to avoid catastrophic forgetting llm · does fine tuning make model worse · fine tuning degrades performance What are instruction tuning, RLHF and DPO? Instruction tuning is supervised fine-tuning on instruction and response pairs so a base model learns to follow requests. RLHF, reinforcement learning from human feedback, then trains a reward model on human preference rankings and optimises the LLM against it, the recipe behind InstructGPT [4]. DPO, direct preference optimisation, reaches a similar result without a separate reward model or reinforcement learning loop by training directly on preferred versus rejected answer pairs [5]. For most teams, supervised fine-tuning first, DPO if you have preference data. Also asked as: what is instruction tuning · what is rlhf · what is rlhf in ai · dpo vs rlhf · dpo vs ppo · dpo vs sft · instruction tuning vs fine tuning · what is preference tuning Three ways to align a modelSupervised fine-tuningRLHFDPODataPrompt and ideal answerPrompt with ranked answers,then a reward modelPrompt with one preferred andone rejected answerComplexityOne training loopReward model plus areinforcement learning loopOne training loop, a speciallossComputeLowestHighestBetween, closer to SFTWhen to useTeaching the task and formatLarge-scale alignment with alabelling teamYou have preference pairs andwant alignment without RLThree ways to align a model TRL ships trainers for all three, and DPO on top of a supervised fine-tune is the practical path for a student project that wants to demonstrate preference tuning [10]. How do I deploy a fine-tuned model? Merge the adapter into the base weights if you want a single artefact, or keep the adapter separate and load it at runtime if you will serve several adapters on one base. Quantise the merged model to GGUF for CPU and consumer-GPU serving with llama.cpp, or to AWQ or GPTQ for GPU servers, then serve with vLLM, llama.cpp, or a Hugging Face endpoint. Keep the exact prompt template from training in the serving code. Also asked as: how to merge lora adapter · merge lora weights · deploy fine tuned llm · serve fine tuned model · fine tuned model to gguf · multi lora serving · vllm lora 3.2 GBVRAM for a QLoRA run on a1.7B model in my write-up2epochs is a sensible defaulton a small dataset16LoRA rank I start from10 to 20%of data held out forevaluationKey numbers Serving multiple LoRA adapters on one base model is how a single GPU can host several fine-tuned behaviours, one per client or per task, which is often the difference between a fine-tuning idea that pays and one that does not. What mistakes do beginners make when fine-tuning? Fine-tuning before trying a better prompt. Training on facts and expecting recall. Using the wrong chat template. Training for ten epochs on a thousand examples. Skipping the validation split. Never comparing with the base model. Quantising before training instead of after. Shipping without the training-time prompt. Each one I have either made or watched a mentee make, and each is cheap to avoid. Also asked as: fine tuning mistakes · common fine tuning errors · why is my fine tuned model bad · fine tuned model gives wrong answers · fine tuning not working The pre-flight list I use before any runPrompting and retrieval already tried and found insufficientSpec written, dataset validated, sample read by eyeChat template applied by the tokenizer, not by handValidation split held outBase model evaluated on the same held-out prompts firstOne variable changed since the last run, and loggedBest checkpoint saved by validation loss, not last checkpointServing code uses the same template as trainingThe pre-flight list I use before any run Is fine-tuning worth it? What does it cost? Compute is the cheap part: a QLoRA run on a small model costs a few GPU hours, which is free on Colab or a few dollars rented. The real costs are the dataset, weeks of a person's time to write and clean examples, and the maintenance, since every requirement change means another run and another evaluation. It is worth it when the behaviour is stable, the volume is high enough that a small fine-tuned model saves inference cost, or no prompt on any model gets the format right. Also asked as: is fine tuning worth it · fine tuning cost estimation · how much does it cost to fine tune an llm · fine tuning roi · fine tuning vs bigger model The honest test I apply before quoting a client: write the twenty examples first. If writing twenty consistent examples is hard, the spec is not ready and the fine-tune will encode the confusion. If it is easy, the fine-tune will probably work, and those twenty become the first rows of the dataset. From my carousel5 Production AI Apps, All Open Source · 8 slides · full deck on Instagram and LinkedIn Where should a student start with fine-tuning? Read the LoRA and QLoRA papers for the idea, then fine-tune a 1 to 2B instruct model on a few hundred examples you wrote yourself, on a free GPU, and compare it with the base model on prompts you held out. Ship the adapter to Hugging Face with a model card that reports the comparison. That single project demonstrates dataset design, training, evaluation and honesty, and it fits in a weekend. Also asked as: fine tuning llm tutorial · how to learn fine tuning · fine tuning course · fine tuning project ideas · fine tuning for beginners · fine tuning roadmap I run sessions on exactly this for college tech clubs, and it is one of the five talks I offer. If your club or hackathon wants one, my email is pranjulrathour41@gmail.com and the details are at pranjulrathour.scult.in/invite.

# How to give a guest lecture in college: preparing a technical talk, handling Q&A, and becoming a speaker colleges invite back
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/how-to-give-a-guest-lecture-in-college/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

How do I get invited to give a guest lecture at a college? Do something specific, describe it in public, and make it easy to book you. Colleges and tech clubs invite people whose credential fits in one sentence, "shipped five production AI apps", "won Changethon at IIT Roorkee", and who have a page or a post that shows what a session with them looks like. Start with your own college and clubs you belong to, offer a concrete topic and two dates, say it is free for students, and post about the first session the same week. The second invitation comes from the first post. Also asked as: how to give guest lecture in college · how to become a guest lecturer in college · how to get invited to speak at colleges · how to become a guest speaker · how to become a campus speaker · how to get speaking opportunities as an engineer · guest lecture opportunities for professionals · how to become a tech speaker My first sessions were at VSICS Kanpur, my own college, to first-years and to the coding club: a career roadmap, a session on AI in the software lifecycle, a debate [1][2][3]. Each one produced a post with photos, each post produced the next invitation, and the pattern has not changed since. A page listing the talks I offer, with formats and logistics, is what organisers now book from [8]. Nobody invites you to talk about AI. They invite you to talk about the thing you built, because you are the only person who can. Pranjul Rathour What should a guest lecture cover? One outcome. Decide what students should be able to do on Monday because of your session, then build backwards. For first-years: a roadmap and permission to start. For second- and third-years: one skill demonstrated live and a project to try. For final-years: what the industry actually hires for and how to show it. A talk that covers a whole topic teaches nothing; a talk that changes one action teaches something. Also asked as: guest lecture topics · topics for guest lecture in engineering college · seminar topics for computer science students · guest lecture topics for cse · how to choose topic for guest lecture · technical talk topics · what to talk about in a college talk · ai topics for guest lecture The same topic, three roomsFirst-yearsSecond- and third-yearsFinal-yearsOutcomeStart one project this monthBuild a RAG demo and join ahackathonFix the portfolio and pass oneinterviewFormat60-minute talk, long Q&amp;A90-minute hands-on withlaptopsTalk plus project clinic ormock interviewsDemoA live app, shown notexplainedStudents run it themselvesReview three student projectson screenWhat to skipJargon and architectureCareer theoryBeginner setupThe same topic, three rooms The three-year roadmap I gave 100+ first-years at the VSICS induction was one outcome: know what year one, two and three are for, and start year one this week [1]. How do I structure a 60- or 90-minute technical talk? Open with a two-minute story that has a failure in it. Show the map: three or four ideas, on one slide, that the session will cover. Do one live demo of something real, ten minutes at most. Give the roadmap: what to do next, in order. Then stop early and take questions for the rest of the slot. Students remember the story, the demo and one line from the roadmap. Slides are cue cards with one idea each; nobody reads paragraphs on a screen. Also asked as: how to structure a technical talk · guest lecture format · how to prepare a technical presentation · how to give a tech talk · talk structure for students · how to make a presentation for guest lecture · how long should a guest lecture be · 90 minute workshop structure The 90-minute session, minute by minute10 to 5: a story with afailure, and who youare in one line25 to 10: the map,three ideas on oneslide310 to 40: the ideas,each with one concreteexample440 to 55: live demo ofa real system,rehearsed555 to 65: the roadmap,what to do next and inwhat order665 to 90: questions,and the hard onesfirstThe 90-minute session, minute by minute My full outline for a 90-minute GenAI session, with the demo and the roadmap slides, is written up on the portfolio [6]. How do I prepare a guest lecture? Ask the organiser five questions: who is in the room and how many, what year, what they already know, what the room has, and what they want students to leave with. Write the one outcome. Build the demo first and rehearse it on the machine you will use. Then write slides, no more than one per two minutes. Rehearse once with a timer, once without slides, and cut a third. Arrive early and test the projector with your laptop. Also asked as: how to prepare for a guest lecture · how to prepare a campus talk · guest lecture preparation · how to prepare a technical talk · presentation preparation checklist · how to rehearse a talk · how to prepare slides for a talk My preparation listFive questions answered by the organiserOne sentence: what students can do on MondayDemo built and rehearsed on the presenting laptop, with a recorded backupSlides: one idea each, readable from the back row, under 30 for 90 minutesStory with a failure written out, not improvisedRoadmap slide with three next steps and linksRehearsed with a timer and cut by a thirdProjector, adapter, Wi-Fi and microphone tested before students arriveMy preparation list The longer version of how I prepare is on the portfolio [4]; the short version is that the demo is built before a single slide exists. How do I handle a quiet room or a difficult question? A quiet room is a setup problem. Ask a question with no wrong answer, "who here has used ChatGPT for an assignment?", raise your own hand, and wait a full five seconds. Take the first answer seriously and build on it. For a question you cannot answer, say so, say what you would check and how, and offer to follow up by email. For a hostile question, restate it calmly, answer the part that is fair, and move on. Students forgive not knowing; they do not forgive bluffing. Also asked as: how to handle q&amp;a after a talk · how to handle questions you don&#x27;t know · how to engage students in a lecture · how to make a guest lecture interactive · how to deal with a quiet audience · how to answer difficult questions in a presentation · public speaking for engineers · how to overcome stage fear for a talk I wrote a separate piece on handling Q&amp;A after technical talks, because it is where most speakers either win or lose the room [5]. The single most useful habit: repeat every question aloud before answering, so the back row hears it and you get three seconds to think. Taking questions during a session Should I use slides, a demo or a whiteboard? All three, in that priority reversed: demo first, whiteboard for the one idea that needs drawing, slides as cue cards. A live demo of a real system is the part students talk about afterwards and the part that proves you have built things. A whiteboard sketch of an architecture lands harder than a diagram slide because they watch it appear. Slides carry structure, links and the roadmap. Never read from them. Also asked as: slides vs demo in a technical talk · how many slides for a 60 minute talk · live demo in presentation tips · should i do a live demo · presentation tips for engineers · how to make technical slides Can you demo something real that works?YESBuild the session around it. Ten minutes of aworking system beats forty of slides.NOBuild the thing first. Speak when you can showit. Until then, mentor one-to-one.Can you demo something real that works? Are guest lecturers paid? Should I charge? Some are, many are not, and universities often have fixed honoraria under their rules. I speak at student communities for free, on-site with travel covered or remote at no cost, because those rooms are where the people I want in the industry sit, and because I was helped the same way. Early on, speak for free and for the post. Later, charge companies and conferences, and keep colleges free if you can. Say your terms in your first reply so nobody is embarrassed. Also asked as: are guest lecturers paid · do guest speakers get paid · how much do guest lecturers earn · guest lecture honorarium · should i charge for speaking at colleges · speaking fee for students · free speaker for college events How do I become a hackathon judge or mentor as well? The same way, one step further: attend hackathons, then mentor at one, then ask the organiser to sit on the panel. Organisers want judges who have built and shipped, who can brief a rubric and who show up on time. Once you have judged once, the invitations come with the speaking ones. Publish your rubric, because organisers copy it and remember where it came from. Also asked as: how to become a hackathon judge · how to get invited as hackathon judge · hackathon mentor how to · how to judge a hackathon · hackathon judge requirements · how to be a good hackathon judge My path from participant to judge, and what organisers told me they look for, is written up separately [7]. What mistakes do first-time speakers make? Covering everything. Reading slides. Forty minutes of context before anything concrete. A demo that has never run on the presenting laptop. No questions asked of the room until the end. Running over time into the next session. Bluffing an answer. Leaving without sharing slides or a way to reach you. Each is fixable before the session with the checklist above; none is fixable during it. Also asked as: common mistakes in guest lectures · presentation mistakes to avoid · public speaking mistakes engineers make · how not to give a boring lecture · technical talk mistakes How speakers usually growLEVEL 1First talkat your own college, onetopic, one demo, survivethe Q&amp;ALEVEL 2Repeat speakertwo or three colleges, apage listing your talksLEVEL 3Workshop leadhands-on sessions wherestudents leave withsomething builtLEVEL 4Judge and mentorpanels, briefings,follow-up mentoringLEVEL 5Voiceorganisers ask you whatstudents need, not theother way roundHow speakers usually grow How do I turn one talk into a lasting relationship with a college? Send the slides and links within a day. Reply to every student email for a month. Post the photos and tag the college and the club. Then propose the next thing: a hands-on workshop, a judging slot at their hackathon, monthly office hours for the club. Three of my longest mentoring relationships with student clubs started as a single session followed by one email I bothered to send. Also asked as: how to build relationships with colleges as a speaker · follow up after guest lecture · mentor relationship with students · how to get repeat speaking invitations · campus speaker relationships 100+first-years in the VSICSinduction session500+members of TechVerseEnclave, the community that1outcome per talk0fee for student communitiesKey numbers Where can I start speaking? At your own college's club, next month, on the thing you built last semester. Offer two dates, one topic and a demo. If you would like to see how I structure sessions, the talk menu and the 90-minute outline are public [6][8]. If your college wants a session, or wants a speaker to show your students how to become speakers, email pranjulrathour41@gmail.com or use pranjulrathour.scult.in/invite. # How to invite a guest speaker to your college: the email, the one-pager, fees, logistics and what makes a speaker say yes
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/how-to-invite-a-guest-speaker-to-your-college/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

How do I invite a guest speaker to my college? Send one clear email with six things: who you are and which club or department you represent, who will be in the room and how many, two or three proposed dates with a time window, the format and duration you want, the topic you hope they will cover and the outcome you want for students, and what you can offer, travel, a certificate, a recording, a meal. Then follow up once after five days. Speakers say yes to invitations that make the decision easy. Also asked as: how to invite a guest speaker to college · how to invite a guest speaker · how to invite a guest lecturer · guest speaker invitation email · how to write invitation for guest lecture · how to ask someone to be a guest speaker · how to invite a speaker for a seminar in college · how to get a guest speaker for college event I receive these invitations regularly, and the ones I accept fastest share a shape. This is the template, written from the receiving end, with what actually decides a yes [1]. "Can you come and speak about AI?" is the most common invitation I get and the hardest to say yes to, because "AI" is not a talk. "Can you run a 90-minute session on building a RAG system for 60 third-years on 12 or 19 October?" is a talk. Pranjul Rathour What should the invitation email say? Subject: "Guest session on [topic] for [college], [month]". Body: one line on who you are, one on the audience, the two dates, the format, the topic and outcome, the offer, and a link to your club's page or last event. Under 200 words. Attach nothing; link instead. Sign with a name, a role and a phone number. Also asked as: guest speaker invitation email sample · invitation letter for guest lecture · guest lecture invitation format · email to invite speaker for webinar · how to write email to guest speaker · invitation for guest speaker template · formal invitation for guest lecture in college Subject: Guest session on GenAI engineering for VSICS Kanpur, October Hi Pranjul, I'm Aditi, secretary of the coding club at VSICS Kanpur. We run monthly sessions for 60 to 80 second- and third-year BCA and B.Tech students. Would you run a 90-minute session on building a RAG system, ending with students having a working demo? Proposed dates: Sat 12 Oct or Sat 19 Oct, 11:00 to 12:30, in our seminar hall (projector, Wi-Fi, 80 seats). We can cover travel within Kanpur, provide a certificate and lunch, and will post photos and a recap tagging you the same week. Last month's session: &lt;link&gt;. Happy to adjust the topic to your menu. Aditi Sharma, Coding Club, VSICS Kanpur, +91 98xxx xxxxx Every sentence answers a question the speaker would otherwise have to ask. That is the whole trick. How do I find a guest speaker for a college event? Start with alumni working in the field, then practitioners in your city, then people who already post about speaking at colleges on LinkedIn. Search LinkedIn for your city plus the topic and "workshop" or "session", check who has spoken at nearby colleges' events, ask community organisers at Google Developer Groups on Campus or Microsoft Learn Student Ambassadors chapters, and look at who judges local hackathons. People who already give their time to students are the ones who will give it to you. Also asked as: how to find guest speakers · how to find a speaker for college event · where to find guest speakers for students · best guest speakers for colleges · guest speaker ideas for college · tech speakers for college events · how to find industry experts for college · speakers for tech fest Where speakers who say yes usually areAlumni two to six years out, in the roles your students wantEngineers at startups and agencies in your cityPeople who post about mentoring, judging or speaking on LinkedInOrganisers and speakers at GDG on Campus and MLSA chapters nearbyHackathon judges and mentors from the last event your students attendedAuthors of blogs your students already readWhere speakers who say yes usually are Community programmes such as Google Developer Groups on Campus and Microsoft Learn Student Ambassadors exist partly to connect chapters with speakers, and their organisers know who is active in your region [6][7]. Major League Hacking's community does the same for hackathon-adjacent speakers [8]. Are guest speakers paid? What does a guest lecturer cost? It varies. Many working engineers, including me, speak at student communities for free, on-site with travel covered or remote at no cost, because that is how we were helped. Professional speakers and senior executives often charge a fee. Universities sometimes have a fixed honorarium for guest lecturers under their academic rules. Ask directly in the first email: "We can offer travel and a certificate; if you have a fee, please tell us." Nobody is offended by that sentence. Also asked as: are guest speakers paid · do guest speakers get paid · do guest lecturers get paid · guest lecturer fee · how much to pay a guest speaker · speaker fee for college event · honorarium for guest lecture · free guest speakers for colleges My own rule: free for student communities and colleges, on-site anywhere in India with travel covered, remote anywhere at no cost [3]. The reason is not generosity; it is that the students in those rooms are exactly the people I want in the community and, later, in the industry. What topics should I ask a speaker to cover? Ask for a topic that ends with students able to do something, not knowing something. "Build a RAG system in 90 minutes", "How hackathon judges score, from a judge", "From BCA to GenAI engineer: the roadmap", "Ship your first AI app for free". Pick from the speaker's own menu if they publish one, and say which of your students it is for: first-years need a roadmap; final-years need a project and interview preparation. Also asked as: seminar topics for computer science students · guest lecture topics for engineering students · workshop topics for college students · ai workshop for students · genai workshop for college · technical seminar topics 2026 · topics for guest lecture in computer science · best seminar topics for cse Matching the talk to the roomFirst-yearsSecond- and third-yearsFinal-yearsFaculty and TPOWhat they needA map and permission tostartA project and acommunityInterview readiness andportfolio reviewCurriculum and industryalignmentFormat that works60-minute talk with Q&amp;A90-minute hands-onworkshopHalf-day project clinicor mock interviews45-minute session plusa discussionTopics from my menuThe three-year roadmapRAG or fine-tuninghands-onShipping AI apps,hackathon strategyWhat the industryactually hires forMatching the talk to the room The five talks I offer, with the audience each is built for, are listed on the portfolio [2]. Most practitioners who speak regularly have a similar page; asking for one of their listed talks gets a faster yes than asking them to invent one. What does a speaker need from the organisers? A one-pager a week before the event: the exact venue and how to reach it, the audience size and year, start and end times, the schedule around their slot, the tech setup, projector input, Wi-Fi, microphone, whiteboard, two contact numbers, and what you will need from them, a bio, a photo, a title. On the day: someone to meet them, water, a working projector tested with their laptop, and a hard stop you protect. Also asked as: guest speaker requirements · what to send a guest speaker before event · guest speaker checklist · how to prepare for guest lecture as organizer · event brief for speaker · speaker logistics checklist · how to host a guest speaker The organiser&#x27;s timeline1Four weeks out:invitation email withdates and topic2Three weeks out:confirm date, collectbio, photo and title3Two weeks out: posterand registration live,speaker tagged4One week out: one-pager sent, tech setupconfirmed5Day before: reminderwith venue pin andcontact numbers6Day of: meet, test theprojector, protect thetime7Same week: photos,recap post, thank-you,and the next askThe organiser&#x27;s timeline The single most common failure I see is the projector: a laptop that will not connect, an adapter nobody has, ten minutes of the session gone. Test with the speaker's actual laptop, or ask them to send slides to run from yours. Taking questions during a session How do I introduce a guest speaker? In under a minute: their name, what they do now, one specific thing they have built or achieved that this audience will respect, why they are here today, and their name again. Do not read their whole LinkedIn. Do not list every award. One concrete credential lands harder than ten adjectives. Also asked as: how to introduce guest speaker · guest speaker introduction sample · how to introduce a guest lecturer in college · introduction speech for guest speaker · how to welcome guest speaker · anchoring script for guest lecture For example: "Pranjul Rathour is a GenAI engineer from Kanpur who shipped five production AI systems this year and won first prize at Changethon at IIT Roorkee. He did his BCA at this college. He's here to show you how a RAG system is actually built. Please welcome Pranjul." Forty seconds, done. What is the difference between a guest lecture, a seminar, a workshop and a webinar? A guest lecture is one expert speaking to a class, usually 45 to 90 minutes with questions. A seminar is a session built around discussion, often with several speakers or student presentations. A workshop is hands-on: students build or practise something with the speaker's guidance, and it needs laptops, more time and a smaller room. A webinar is any of these delivered online. Ask for the format that matches your goal: a lecture to inspire, a workshop to equip. Also asked as: difference between guest lecture and seminar · difference between workshop and guest lecture · difference between webinar and guest lecture · what is guest lecture · what is guest lecturer · guest lecture vs seminar vs workshop · types of college events Choosing the formatGuest lectureWorkshopWebinarLength45 to 90 minutes2 to 4 hours45 to 60 minutesRoomAuditorium, any sizeLab or classroom, laptops, 30to 60 peopleNoneOutcomeStudents know something andare motivatedStudents can do something andhave a demoReach beyond campus, recordingSpeaker prepSlidesSlides plus setup instructionssent in advanceSlides plus a stableconnectionCost and effortLowestHighest, but the highest valueLowChoosing the format How do I get a speaker for a remote or online session? The same email, minus travel, plus the platform you will use and whether you will record. Remote sessions are the easiest yes a speaker can give, so use them for speakers outside your city, for shorter formats and for follow-ups after an in-person session. Test the platform with the speaker for five minutes the day before, assign a moderator to read questions, and send the recording link within a week. Also asked as: how to invite speaker for webinar · online guest lecture · remote guest lecture tips · how to organize webinar in college · virtual guest speaker · how to host online session for students I speak remotely for any student community anywhere at no cost, which is true of many practitioners; the constraint is never the speaker's willingness, it is whether the invitation is concrete [3]. How do I turn one session into a lasting relationship? Post the photos and a recap the same week, tagging the speaker and the college. Send a two-line thank-you with one thing students did as a result. Then ask for the next specific thing: judging your hackathon, a follow-up workshop, an office-hours call for the club, feedback on three student projects. Speakers remember organisers who follow through, and the second yes is always faster than the first. Also asked as: how to build relationship with guest speaker · follow up email after guest lecture · thank you email to guest speaker · how to get speaker to come again · guest speaker feedback form · mentor relationship after guest lecture Three of my longest mentoring relationships with student clubs started as one session; what they had in common was an organiser who wrote back a week later with photos and a question. 6things every invitationemail needs200words is enough for thefirst email1week before is when the one-pager should arrive0fee I charge studentcommunitiesKey numbers What mistakes do organisers make? Vague topics. One date offered with no alternative. Asking two days before the event. No mention of the audience. Attachments instead of links. Forgetting to say whether the session is online or on-site. Not testing the projector. Ending late and eating into the speaker's next commitment. Never posting afterwards. Each is fixed by the checklist above, and each one I have experienced as a speaker. # How to learn Python for AI in 2026: the roadmap from zero to shipping an LLM app, what to skip, and the projects that prove it
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/how-to-learn-python-for-ai/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

How do I learn Python for AI? Learn the Python that ships software, then point it at models. In practice: variables, functions and data structures; reading and writing files and JSON; calling HTTP APIs; virtual environments and packages; classes when you need them; async when you have many calls; tests. Then, with that base, call a model API, build a small FastAPI service around it, and deploy it. Twelve weeks of building gets a beginner to a live LLM application. Twelve weeks of tutorials gets a beginner to week thirteen of tutorials. Also asked as: how to learn python for ai · python for ai · python for machine learning beginners · learn python for artificial intelligence · python roadmap for ai · how much python is needed for ai · python for genai · python for llm development · best way to learn python for ai · python for data science vs ai All five production AI systems I shipped in 2026 are Python services: a RAG platform, a fine-tuning platform, a document extraction service, a face recognition backend and an OCR and speech workspace [14]. The Python inside them is not exotic. It is the Python in this roadmap, used carefully, with tests. Nobody has ever asked me to reverse a linked list in Python at work. Everybody has asked me why the API call timed out. Learn for the second question. Pranjul Rathour How much Python do I need for AI? Less than the tutorials suggest, and different. You need: core syntax and data structures; functions with type hints; modules and packages; file and JSON handling; error handling; HTTP requests; virtual environments; the standard library's pathlib, json, datetime, logging and asyncio; classes and dataclasses; and writing tests. You do not need, at first: metaclasses, decorators beyond using them, deep NumPy, or competitive-programming tricks. Those come when a project demands them. Also asked as: how much python for machine learning · python level needed for ai · do i need to master python for ai · what python concepts for ai · python basics for machine learning · is basic python enough for ai · advanced python for ai · python topics for ai engineer The Python an AI engineer uses dailyFunctions with type hints and docstringsLists, dicts, sets, comprehensionsReading and writing files, JSON, CSVtry, except, and raising clear errorsrequests or httpx for HTTP, with timeoutsVirtual environments and a lock filepathlib, json, datetime, logging, asyncio from the standard librarydataclasses or Pydantic models for structured datapytest for testsReading a traceback calmlyThe Python an AI engineer uses daily What is the roadmap from zero to an AI app? Twelve weeks, four projects, each deployed. Weeks one to three: fundamentals through a command-line tool that reads a file and produces a report. Weeks four to six: HTTP and APIs through a script that calls a model API and saves structured output. Weeks seven to nine: a FastAPI service with a database, deployed on a free tier. Weeks ten to twelve: a RAG application over documents you know, with an evaluation set. Every week, one commit a day, and a README that explains what you built. Also asked as: python roadmap for ai 2026 · python learning path for ai · python for ai step by step · 3 month python roadmap · python to machine learning roadmap · how long to learn python for ai · python projects for ai beginners · python for ai course Twelve weeks, four deployed projects1Weeks 1 to 3: syntax,functions, files, JSON2ship a CLI report tool3Weeks 4 to 6: HTTP,APIs, error handling4ship a script thatcalls a model andsaves JSON5Weeks 7 to 9: FastAPI,Postgres, Docker6ship a service on afree tier7Weeks 10 to 12: a RAGapp over yourdocuments with a20-question eval set8Every week: one commita day, a README, ashort postTwelve weeks, four deployed projects The longer version, with resources per week, is on the portfolio [13]. Which Python libraries matter for AI in 2026? For calling models: the provider SDKs, or plain httpx and requests [5][6]. For services: FastAPI with Pydantic for validation [4][7]. For data handling: json and pathlib from the standard library, pandas when tables appear. For retrieval: an embeddings client and pgvector or FAISS. For training and fine-tuning: PyTorch, Transformers, PEFT and TRL, learned when you fine-tune, not before. For tests: pytest [8]. For environments: uv or venv with pip [9]. Learn each when a project needs it. Also asked as: python libraries for ai · best python libraries for machine learning · python libraries for llm · python libraries for genai · langchain vs openai sdk · fastapi for ai · pydantic for llm · python ai stack 2026 · essential python packages for ai Libraries by the job they doJobLibraryWhen to learn itCall a modelProvider SDK, httpxWeek 4Validate data and outputsPydanticWeek 4Build an APIFastAPIWeek 7Store datapsycopg or SQLAlchemy withPostgresWeek 7Retrievalpgvector or FAISS, anembeddings clientWeek 10Notebooks and GPUsJupyter, ColabWeek 10Fine-tuningPyTorch, Transformers, PEFT,TRLAfter the first RAG appTestspytestWeek 2, and alwaysLibraries by the job they do Frameworks such as LangChain are fine for a first prototype; I recommend calling the SDKs directly for your first real project so you understand every line you ship. Should I learn NumPy, pandas and maths first? No, not first. For an applications career in GenAI, you can build and deploy your first LLM app without NumPy. Learn pandas when you have a table to analyse, NumPy when you touch vectors directly, and the maths, linear algebra and probability, alongside your first embedding and fine-tuning projects, where it has a purpose. Learning them first is how students spend six months on prerequisites and never ship. For a research or classical ML path, reverse the order. Also asked as: numpy for ai · do i need numpy for ai · pandas for machine learning · maths for python ai · linear algebra for ai · should i learn maths before ai · data science prerequisites · do i need statistics for genai Do you want to build AI applications or train and researchmodels?YESApplications: Python, APIs, FastAPI, a deployedproject first. Maths and NumPy when the projectneeds them.NOResearch: maths, NumPy, PyTorch fundamentalsfirst, then the applications layer.Do you want to build AI applications or train and research models? What are the best free resources to learn Python for AI? The official Python tutorial for the language itself [1]. Automate the Boring Stuff for practical scripting [2]. Python for Everybody for a gentle structured course [3]. FastAPI's documentation, which is a course in itself [4]. Hugging Face's free LLM course once you are calling models [10]. fast.ai for deep learning intuition when you get there [11]. Google Colab for a free notebook and GPU [12]. All free. Pick one per stage, finish it by building, and do not collect courses. Also asked as: best free resources to learn python for ai · free python course for ai · python for ai youtube · learn python free 2026 · best python books for ai · python for everybody · automate the boring stuff · python course for beginners free A career session for students What should my first Python AI project be? A script that reads a folder of your own notes or PDFs, calls a model API to summarise each one into structured JSON, validates the JSON with Pydantic, and writes a report. It touches files, HTTP, error handling, structured data and tests, and it is useful to you. Then wrap it in FastAPI and deploy it. Then add retrieval so you can ask questions across the notes. Three steps, three months, one growing project, live at a URL. Also asked as: first python ai project · python ai project ideas for beginners · simple ai project in python · python llm project · python project ideas 2026 · mini project python ai · python chatbot project · beginner genai project python import json from pathlib import Path from pydantic import BaseModel class Summary(BaseModel): title: str key_points: list[str] open_questions: list[str] def summarise(path: Path) -&gt; Summary: text = path.read_text(encoding=&quot;utf-8&quot;) raw = call_model(f&quot;Summarise into JSON with title, key_points, open_questions:\n\n{text}&quot;) return Summary.model_validate_json(raw) # fails loudly if the model drifts report = [summarise(p).model_dump() for p in Path(&quot;notes&quot;).glob(&quot;*.md&quot;)] Path(&quot;report.json&quot;).write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding=&quot;utf-8&quot;) That is a week-four project, and a version of it is the seed of every document system I have shipped. What mistakes keep students stuck in Python tutorials? Watching instead of typing. Starting a fourth course before deploying a first project. Learning NumPy for months before calling a single API. Skipping virtual environments and losing a week to dependency conflicts. Never writing a test, so every change is scary. Copying assistant output without reading it. Treating tracebacks as failures instead of instructions. The fix for all of them is the same: ship something small every week and read the errors. Also asked as: why i can&#x27;t learn python · stuck in tutorial hell python · python learning mistakes · how to get out of tutorial hell · python beginner mistakes · learning python too slow · python practice for ai Python for AI interview questions Expect practical Python: parse and validate JSON, write a retry with backoff around an API call, chunk text by paragraphs with a size cap, compute cosine similarity, use a dict to count or group, write a small async fan-out over many API calls, and write a test for one of those. Rarely puzzles. Interviewers want typed, readable code and a candidate who talks through edge cases; the coding round for GenAI roles is a work sample, not an exam. Also asked as: python interview questions for ai engineer · python coding interview genai · python questions for machine learning interview · python for ai interview preparation · async python interview · python typing interview 12weeks from zero to adeployed AI app, if you ship4projects, each live at a URL5production Python AIservices I shipped in six0linked lists reversed atworkKey numbers How Python skill actually growsLEVEL 1Scriptsfiles, JSON, a CLI toolthat does one jobLEVEL 2APIsHTTP calls with timeouts,structured outputs, testsLEVEL 3ServicesFastAPI, a database,Docker, deployedLEVEL 4Systemsretrieval, async,logging, cost control,evaluationLEVEL 5Craftreading other people&#x27;scode and making yourseasy to readHow Python skill actually grows From my carousel15 Free Tools, No Signup, Every Link · 9 slides · full deck on Instagram and LinkedIn Where should I start today? Install Python, create a virtual environment, and write a script that reads one file and prints a summary of it. Tomorrow make the summary come from a model API. By the weekend, put it in a repository with a README. # How to prepare a dataset for fine-tuning an LLM: formats, chat templates, how much data, synthetic data, validation and the checklist before you train
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/how-to-prepare-a-dataset-for-fine-tuning/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

How do I prepare a dataset for fine-tuning an LLM? Start with a written spec of the behaviour you want, then collect or write examples that follow it exactly: for each, the input a user would give and the ideal output, in the chat format the base model expects. Deduplicate, validate every row against the spec, hold out a validation split, measure token lengths, and read a random sample by eye. The dataset is the fine-tune; the training run only copies what is in it, including its inconsistencies. Also asked as: how to prepare dataset for fine tuning · how to create dataset for llm fine tuning · fine tuning dataset preparation · dataset for fine tuning llm · how to make training data for llm · fine tuning data format · llm training data preparation · how to build a fine tuning dataset FineTune Studio, the platform I built in 2026, validates the uploaded dataset before it lets a run start, because the most common reason a run produced a bad model had nothing to do with hyper-parameters: the data was inconsistent, mis-templated or leaked into the validation split [12]. This page is that validation, explained. Write twenty examples by hand before anything else. If twenty consistent examples are hard to write, the spec is not ready, and the fine-tune will faithfully learn the confusion. Pranjul Rathour, from building FineTune Studio What should the spec contain? One paragraph: who the user is, what they send, what the model must produce, in what format, with what tone, and what it must do when the input is unclear or out of scope. Then three example pairs that follow it. Every later example is checked against this paragraph. A spec you cannot write in a paragraph is a task you are not ready to train. Also asked as: fine tuning task specification · how to define fine tuning task · what behavior to fine tune · fine tuning goals · fine tuning requirements document Which dataset format should I use: Alpaca, ShareGPT or chat messages? Use the messages format, a list of role and content turns, system, user, assistant, because it maps directly onto the chat template every modern model uses and onto what TRL's trainer expects [7]. Alpaca's instruction, input and output fields [1] and ShareGPT's multi-turn conversations are older JSON shapes that convert to messages trivially. The format is a container; what the model actually sees is the template rendered from it. Also asked as: alpaca format vs sharegpt format · alpaca dataset format · sharegpt format · chatml format · fine tuning dataset json format · jsonl format for fine tuning · openai fine tuning format · conversational dataset format · instruction dataset format The three common shapesAlpacaShareGPTMessages (chat)Fieldsinstruction, input, outputconversations with from andvaluemessages with role and contentMulti-turnNoYesYesSystem promptImplicitSometimesExplicitMaps to chat templatesNeeds conversionNeeds conversionDirectlyUse it whenReproducing older recipesImporting existingconversation dataEverything newThe three common shapes A row in the messages format, which is also the shape most APIs accept [9]: {&quot;messages&quot;: [ {&quot;role&quot;: &quot;system&quot;, &quot;content&quot;: &quot;You are a support agent for Acme. Answer only from the provided policy. If the policy does not cover the question, say so and offer to escalate.&quot;}, {&quot;role&quot;: &quot;user&quot;, &quot;content&quot;: &quot;Policy: Refunds within 14 days with receipt.\n\nQuestion: I bought it 20 days ago, can I return it?&quot;}, {&quot;role&quot;: &quot;assistant&quot;, &quot;content&quot;: &quot;The policy allows refunds within 14 days of purchase with a receipt, so a return at 20 days is outside the window. I can escalate this to a supervisor if you would like.&quot;} ]} What is a chat template and why does it matter? A chat template is the exact string layout a model was trained on for conversations: the special tokens that mark the start and end of each turn and which role speaks. Every model family uses a different one. If you train with the wrong template, or hand-write the tokens with a small mistake, the model learns garbage or produces it at inference. Always render examples with the tokenizer's own template function [6], and use the same template when you serve the model. Also asked as: chat template fine tuning · what is chat template · apply chat template hugging face · chatml vs llama template · special tokens fine tuning · eos token fine tuning · template mismatch fine tuning · how to format prompts for fine tuning from transformers import AutoTokenizer tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(BASE) text = tok.apply_chat_template(row[&quot;messages&quot;], tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=False) # never build this string by hand; the template lives with the model Template mismatch is the single most common cause of a fine-tuned chat model that "does not work", in my experience and in the support questions FineTune Studio users asked. My longer note on formats and templates is on the portfolio [11]. How much data do I need to fine-tune an LLM? For tone, style and output format: a few hundred high-quality examples produce a visible, stable change. For a classification or extraction skill: a few thousand covering the classes and the edge cases. For adapting to a domain's language: tens of thousands. Below about a hundred, put the examples in the prompt instead. LIMA showed that a thousand carefully curated examples were enough to teach strong instruction-following, and that quality mattered more than quantity [2]. Also asked as: how much data to fine tune llm · minimum dataset size for fine tuning · how many examples for fine tuning · fine tuning with small dataset · dataset size for lora · how many samples for qlora · fine tuning with 100 examples · fine tuning with 1000 examples Rough data needs by goalGoalExamplesNotesStyle, tone, voice200 to 1,000Consistency is everythingStrict output format, JSONschema300 to 2,000Cover every field and everyedge caseClassification orextraction1,000 to 10,000Balance the classes, includehard negativesDomain adaptation10,000 and upMix in general data to limitforgettingNew reasoning skillUncertain and often notachievableConsider a stronger base modelfirstRough data needs by goal These are orders of magnitude from experience, not laws; the only reliable number comes from training on half your data and checking whether the other half still improves the model. Can I use synthetic data for fine-tuning? Yes, and most fine-tuning datasets today are partly synthetic: a stronger model generates examples from your spec, from seed examples, or from documents. Self-Instruct and Alpaca showed the approach at scale [3][1]. It works when you filter hard: validate every generated row against the spec, remove duplicates and near-duplicates, spot-check by hand, and mix in real examples so the model does not learn the generator's tics and refusals. Unfiltered synthetic data teaches a copy of the generator, not your task. Also asked as: synthetic data for fine tuning · how to generate training data with llm · synthetic dataset generation llm · is synthetic data good for fine tuning · self instruct · data augmentation for llm fine tuning · llm generated training data quality Generating synthetic examples safely1Write the spec and 20human examples2Prompt a strong modelwith the spec and 3 to5 examples to producemore3Generate diverseinputs first, thenoutputs, to avoidrepetition4Validate each rowagainst the specautomatically wherepossible5Deduplicate onnormalised text and onembeddings6Read a random 50 byhand, reject patternsyou dislike7Mix with realexamples, at least aquarter real if youhave themGenerating synthetic examples safely How do I clean and deduplicate the dataset? Normalise whitespace and encoding. Remove exact duplicates, then near-duplicates by comparing normalised text or embeddings, because duplicated training data both wastes compute and makes models memorise [5]. Remove rows that violate the spec: wrong format, wrong language, refusals you did not intend, outputs that reference the prompt. Strip personal data you do not have consent to train on. Measure token lengths and trim or split outliers so no row exceeds your training sequence length. Also asked as: dataset cleaning for fine tuning · deduplicate training data · data quality for llm training · remove duplicates from dataset · dataset validation llm · training data quality checks · how to clean text data for fine tuning Validation before trainingEvery row parses and has the required rolesRendered with the tokenizer&#x27;s template, no hand-written tokensExact and near-duplicates removedNo row exceeds max sequence lengthOutputs follow the spec&#x27;s format, checked by code where possiblePersonal data removed or consentedClass balance measured for classification tasksRandom sample of 50 read by a humanValidation split held out and never trained onValidation before training The Hugging Face Datasets library handles the mechanics, loading, mapping, filtering and splitting, for datasets of any size [8]. My own pre-training validation checklist, which FineTune Studio runs automatically, is written up separately [10]. Requirements gathering and user flows, on stage How do I split training and validation data? Hold out ten to twenty percent, chosen so that near-duplicates of a training row never land in validation, or the validation loss lies to you. For grouped data, all rows from one document, one user or one conversation go to the same split. Keep a third, small test set of examples you wrote by hand and never look at during tuning, for the final honest comparison of base versus fine-tuned. Also asked as: train validation split fine tuning · how to split dataset for llm · validation set for fine tuning · test set for llm evaluation · data leakage fine tuning · holdout set llm What is label masking, and should I train on the user turns? Label masking means computing the loss only on the assistant's tokens, so the model learns to produce answers rather than to predict the user's questions. Most trainers do this for you when you use the messages format with a chat template and an assistant-only loss option [7]. Training on user turns wastes capacity and can teach the model to continue user text. Mask them unless you have a specific reason not to. Also asked as: label masking fine tuning · train on completions only · assistant only loss · loss on user tokens · completion only training · sft loss masking What are common dataset mistakes? Mixing two specs in one dataset, so the model learns to flip between them. Hand-writing chat tokens. Duplicated rows inflating confidence. A validation split that shares documents with training. Outputs that mention the instruction. Ten variations of the same easy example and none of the hard cases. Personal data nobody consented to. Not reading any rows. A model can only be as consistent as its data, and it will be exactly as inconsistent. Also asked as: fine tuning dataset mistakes · common data mistakes llm training · why fine tuned model is bad data · bad training data examples · fine tuning data pitfalls 20examples to write by handbefore anything else1,000curated examples was enoughin LIMA10 to 20percent held out forvalidation50rows to read by eye beforepressing trainKey numbers Dataset interview questions How much data do you need for a style fine-tune versus a skill? What is a chat template and what happens if you get it wrong? How do you generate synthetic data without teaching the generator's habits? How do you prevent leakage between splits? What is label masking? Each answer above is a paragraph; the best evidence is a dataset you built and a model whose behaviour you can trace to specific rows. Also asked as: fine tuning dataset interview questions · llm data preparation interview · training data interview questions From my carousel5 Production AI Apps, All Open Source · 8 slides · full deck on Instagram and LinkedIn Where should I start? Pick one narrow behaviour, write the paragraph spec and twenty examples tonight, render them with the tokenizer's template, and read them back. Then generate two hundred more synthetically, filter them against the spec, and hold out twenty. That dataset will fine-tune a small model on a free GPU tomorrow. For a hands-on fine-tuning workshop at your college, email pranjulrathour41@gmail.com or use pranjulrathour.scult.in/invite.
