# How to start a tech community on campus: from five friends to 500 members, the sessions, the structure and the mistakes, from building TechVerse Enclave
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/how-to-start-a-tech-community-on-campus/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

How do I start a tech community on campus? Pick one topic you can teach for an hour, book a room, tell five people, and run the session this week. Then run one next week. A community is a weekly session that happens whether five or fifty people attend; everything else, the name, the logo, the group chat, the sponsors, comes after the habit exists. TechVerse Enclave started in 2023 as a hackathon team and a handful of friends learning web development together. It has since grown past 500 members, and I have mentored more than 200 students through it. The first six months were the hardest and the most important. Also asked as: how to start a tech community on campus · how to start a coding club in college · how to build a developer community · how to start a tech club · student community building · how to create a college tech community · starting a programming club · how to grow a tech community The full playbook, with the timeline and the numbers, is on the portfolio [1][3]. This page is the version for someone starting Monday. Nobody joins a community. They come to a session, and they come back to the next one because it happened. The community is the coming back. Pranjul Rathour, founder of TechVerse Enclave What should the first session be? Something you built last month, shown live, then a hands-on hour where everyone leaves with a version running. A first session about "introduction to AI" attracts fifty curious people who never return. A first session where ten people deploy their first web page attracts ten people who return with friends. Teach what you know; the second session can be taught by whoever learned fastest. Also asked as: first session for a tech club · tech club session ideas · what to teach in coding club · beginner workshop ideas for college · first coding club meeting · how to run a workshop for students The first month1Week 1: one topic, oneroom, five people, alive demo and a hands-on hour2Week 2: same time,same room, the nextstep of the same topic3Week 3: a memberteaches something theylearned4Week 4: a small buildday: two hours,everyone ships onething5Every week: photos anda two-line post thesame dayThe first month The session format I still use, with timings, is written up separately [4]: ten minutes of story, twenty of demonstration, forty of hands-on, and a public artefact from every attendee. How do I get people to show up and keep coming? Same time, same place, every week, announced the day before, with photos and a recap the same day. Make the first-timer's experience good: someone greets them, the setup instructions were sent in advance, they leave with something working. Ask every attendee to bring one person. Celebrate small ships publicly. Growth came for TechVerse Enclave when members started teaching, because each new teacher brought their own circle. Also asked as: how to increase participation in tech club · how to grow a college club · student engagement tech community · how to retain members in a community · how to promote a coding club · how to make a tech club active How should a student community be organised? Small roles with names: a lead, a sessions lead who owns the calendar, a content lead who posts, an outreach lead who invites speakers and talks to faculty, and a treasurer if money exists. A shared calendar planned a month ahead. A written handover document from day one, because the founders graduate. A faculty coordinator who signs forms and books rooms, kept informed monthly. Nothing more until the weekly session has run for a semester. Also asked as: tech club structure · roles in a coding club · how to organize a student tech community · club leadership structure · how to manage a college club · student club governance · how to hand over a club to juniors The structure that survives graduationFive named roles, each with one responsibilityA monthly calendar published in advanceA handover document that a new lead could run the club fromA faculty coordinator kept informedA single public channel for announcements and a private one for organisersA repository of past session materialsA yearly election or nomination for the next leadsPhotos and posts archived somewhere that outlives any one accountThe structure that survives graduation The mistake that kills most college clubs is not low attendance; it is a founding batch that graduates without a handover. The lessons post covers what I got wrong here first [2]. How do I get speakers, mentors and judges? Invite practitioners with a concrete ask: a topic from their own work, two dates, the audience, the format, what you offer. Start with alumni and engineers in your city, then people who already post about speaking at colleges. Many, including me, speak for free for student communities. Build a record first: a speaker says yes faster to a community with photos of ten past sessions than to one with a plan. Then ask each speaker for the next thing, judging your hackathon, monthly office hours. Also asked as: how to get speakers for college tech club · how to invite industry experts to college · guest speakers for student community · how to find mentors for a coding club · how to get hackathon judges · industry connect for tech club My detailed guide to writing the invitation is a separate page on this site; the short version is six things in one email and a follow-up after five days. In a packed college auditorium How do I run a hackathon as a student community? Start with a 12-hour internal build day for your own members, then a one-day campus hackathon, then a bigger one with outside teams. Fix the rubric and the timeline before you fix the theme. Recruit judges who have built things and brief them for fifteen minutes. Protect the demo slot: three minutes each, a hard stop, a working projector. Sponsors come after the first successful event, not before. TechVerse Enclave's first hackathon was an afternoon in a classroom; the ones after had partners because the first one had photos. Also asked as: how to organize a hackathon in college · how to run a college hackathon · hackathon organizer guide · how to host a hackathon · hackathon planning checklist · college hackathon budget · how to get sponsors for hackathon · hackathon judging rubric for organizers The organiser guide with the timeline, rubric and budget lines is on the portfolio [5]. How do I get sponsors, funding and partner programmes? Programmes first, money second. Google Developer Groups on Campus, Microsoft Learn Student Ambassadors, the GitHub Campus Program and Major League Hacking give student communities structure, resources, swag, speakers and credibility, for free [6][7][8][9]. Apply once you have a semester of sessions to show. Local companies sponsor food and prizes for hackathons when you show them last year's photos and this year's plan. College funding follows visible activity, so make the activity visible first. Also asked as: how to get sponsors for college tech club · funding for student tech community · gdg on campus how to apply · microsoft learn student ambassador program · github campus program benefits · mlh for college clubs · tech club sponsorship How does a community help your career? In every way that a certificate does not. My teammates for three winning hackathons came from it. My first clients came from it. The sessions I ran inside it became the sessions colleges invited me to give. The people I mentored became referrals. Recruiters read "founded a 500-member developer community and mentored 200 students" as leadership evidence no course provides. And teaching every week is the fastest way to actually understand what you are learning. # How to win a hackathon: what judges score, how to pick an idea, and the demo that works live, from three first prizes
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/how-to-win-a-hackathon/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

What is a hackathon? A hackathon is a timed competition, usually 24 to 48 hours, sometimes a few weeks online, where small teams build a working prototype that solves a stated problem and then pitch it to judges. The output is a demo, not a plan. The prize is usually cash, credits or an incubation offer, but the lasting value is the project, the repository and the people you built it with. Also asked as: what is hackathon · what is hackathon and how does it work · what is hackathon competition · what is hackathon in engineering college · what is hackathon for beginners · hackathon meaning · what is college hackathon · what is ai hackathon The word blends "hack", in the sense of building something quickly, with "marathon". In India the format ranges from a two-day event in a college seminar hall to Smart India Hackathon, the government-run national competition with a months-long process [1]. AI hackathons are the same format with problem statements that expect a model, an agent or a data pipeline in the solution. I have been on both sides of the table: three first prizes as a builder, at IIT Roorkee, CSJMU Kanpur and MeetKats, a loss I learned more from than any win, and time as a judge and mentor at college events. This page is the version of the talk I give students, with the parts that made the difference between winning and not. Every hackathon I won, we solved a smaller problem than the teams we beat. Every hackathon I lost, we tried to solve a bigger one. Pranjul Rathour How does a hackathon work? Registration opens weeks ahead. Teams form, usually two to five people. On the day, organisers reveal or confirm the problem statements, the timer starts, and teams build. Mentors circulate. At the end, each team submits code and a short deck and gets a few minutes to demo and answer questions. Judges score against a rubric, and prizes follow. Also asked as: how hackathon works · how does a hackathon work · hackathon process · hackathon rules · what happens in a hackathon · hackathon timeline A 36-hour hackathon, hour by hour1Hour 0 to 2: pick theproblem, cut scope,assign roles2Hour 2 to 6: skeletonapp with the demo pathstubbed end to end3Hour 6 to 20: buildthe one feature thedemo needs, nothingelse4Hour 20 to 26: sleepin shifts, integrate,fix the demo path5Hour 26 to 32: deck,script, rehearse thedemo three times6Hour 32 to 36: freezethe code, record abackup video, pitchA 36-hour hackathon, hour by hour The single most important line in that timeline is "skeleton with the demo path stubbed end to end" in the first six hours. A team that can click through a fake version of the final demo at hour 6 will have a real one at hour 30. A team that builds features in isolation integrates at hour 33 and demos a crash. How do I find and join a hackathon in India? Devfolio and Unstop list most Indian college and company hackathons, Major League Hacking lists student events worldwide, Devpost covers global online ones, and Smart India Hackathon runs through colleges via its official portal. Follow the tech clubs of IITs, NITs and nearby colleges on Instagram and LinkedIn, because campus hackathons are announced there first. Register early; good events fill. Also asked as: how to find hackathons · how to find hackathons in india · how to join hackathon · how to participate in hackathon · how to join online hackathon · best hackathons in india · upcoming hackathons · hackathons for students in india · how to find online hackathons · best online hackathons · hackathon websites Where Indian students find hackathonsDevfolioUnstopMLHDevpostSmart India HackathonWhat it listsCollege andcommunityhackathons, manyCollegecompetitions, casestudies andStudent hackathonsworldwide, aseason calendarGlobal onlinehackathons, oftencompany-runOne national eventwith governmentproblem statementsBest forFirst campushackathon,building aVolume, filtersfor eligibilityand locationOnlineparticipation withinternationalAI and API-specificchallenges withA serious multi-month team projectCostFreeFreeFreeFreeFreeWhere Indian students find hackathons Sources for these listings are the platforms themselves [2][3][4][5]. My recommendation for a first-year: one campus hackathon within a two-hour train ride, in person, before any online one. You learn more from watching thirty teams demo in one room than from a month of tutorials. Can a beginner participate in a hackathon? Yes, and you should, before you feel ready. Most college hackathons have a beginner track or no prerequisites at all. Join a team where one person can already build a basic web or Python app, take the role that matches what you can do, design, research, presentation, testing, and build the skill of finishing under a deadline. Nobody is judged on their first hackathon; they are judged on their demo. Also asked as: hackathon for beginners · how to do hackathon for beginners · how to prepare for hackathon for beginners · can a beginner participate in hackathon · hackathon for first year students · how to learn hackathon · what to learn for hackathon How do I pick a hackathon idea that can win? Pick a problem a specific person has, that you can demonstrate end to end in three minutes, where the hardest part is something your team can actually build in the time you have. Start from the problem statement's audience, list five problems that person has, choose the one with the clearest before-and-after, and cut everything that is not on the path from the user's pain to your demo. Also asked as: hackathon ideas · best hackathon project ideas · hackathon project ideas · how to find hackathon ideas · ai hackathon ideas · hackathon ideas for beginners · unique hackathon ideas · cool hackathon ideas · hackathon ideas for students · 2026 hackathon ideas Ideas that won for us, and why: KrishGyan, Changethon 2025 at IIT Roorkee. Farming advice in the farmer's own voice and language over WhatsApp: pest control, crop health and weather, spoken back, no reading or typing needed. It won because the demo was a voice note in and a voice note out, which any judge could follow, and because the audience was real and underserved [6]. BrandHive, Product Genesis at CSJMU Kanpur. A platform for small businesses and emerging influencers to grow organically without a marketing budget. It won because we showed the whole loop, not a slide of features [7]. Annapurna, BYTEBATTLE by MeetKats. Coordinating surplus food between donors, NGOs and volunteers, with four roles and a verified-impact layer. It won on clarity of roles and a demo that walked one meal from a hotel kitchen to a shelter [8]. And the one that did not: STROT, where we built more and explained less, and a simpler team took the prize [9]. That loss is why every timeline I give now starts with cutting scope. Idea test before you commitOne sentence names the user and their painThe demo path is under three minutes and you can describe every clickThe hardest technical piece is something a team member has done before or can learn in two hoursIt maps to at least three of the four judging criteriaA judge with no context would understand the before-and-afterThere is a plausible next step after the hackathonIdea test before you commit What are good AI hackathon project ideas? The winning AI ideas apply a model to one narrow workflow with real inputs: voice-first advice for people who do not type, document extraction for a specific paper form, a RAG assistant over one institution's documents, a vision check for one quality problem, an agent that completes one repetitive task end to end. "ChatGPT for X" loses to "this one task, done, with this evidence". Also asked as: ai hackathon project ideas · best ai project for hackathon · generative ai hackathon ideas · llm hackathon ideas · machine learning hackathon ideas · ai based hackathon ideas · hackathon ideas using chatgpt A frame that produces ideas fast: pick an audience, farmers, first-year students, small shops, clinics, college offices; pick a friction, a form, a queue, a language barrier, a lost document; ask what the AI removes. KrishGyan came out of exactly that frame: farmers, the reading barrier, voice. What do hackathon judges actually look for? Judges score four things, whatever the rubric calls them: feasibility, does it work and could it exist; innovation, is there a real insight, not just a new coat of paint; practicality, would the stated user actually use it; and problem solving, did you understand the problem before you built. Presentation and teamwork are usually smaller weights. A working demo of a modest idea beats a slide deck of a grand one every time. Also asked as: hackathon judging criteria · what do hackathon judges look for · hackathon rubric · how are hackathons judged · hackathon evaluation criteria · hackathon judging parameters · how to impress hackathon judges A judging rubric I have used, and how to earn each pointCriterionWhat the judge asksWhat earns the marksFeasibilityDoes it run, and could it runfor realLive demo without a crash,honest architecture slideInnovationWhat is the insight othersmissedOne sharp idea stated in onesentencePracticalityWould the user adopt ittomorrowReal users named, constraintsrespected, cost consideredProblem solvingDid they understand theproblemEvidence you talked to orobserved the userPresentation: Can I follow itin three minutesStory, demo, ask, in thatorderA judging rubric I have used, and how to earn each point These four criteria, feasibility, innovation, practicality and problem solving, are the ones I put on the screen when I brief a room as a judge, and the ones I wrote about after sitting on panels [10]. The weights change; the questions do not. Walking a room through evaluation criteria What questions do judges ask in Q&amp;A? Who is this for and have you spoken to them? What happens when this fails? How is this different from the existing solution? What would you build next with a month? Which part did you write yourselves versus take from a library? Judges use Q&amp;A to find out whether you understand your own project, so short honest answers beat confident vague ones. Also asked as: hackathon questions judges ask · hackathon qna · how to answer hackathon judges · what to say to hackathon judges How do I pitch a hackathon project? In three minutes: thirty seconds on who has the problem and what it costs them, ninety seconds of live demo on the happy path, thirty seconds on how it works with one architecture slide, and thirty seconds on what you would do next and what you are asking for. Say the user's name, not the technology's, in the first sentence. Rehearse it three times with a timer. Also asked as: how to present hackathon idea · hackathon pitch · best hackathon pitch · hackathon presentation · hackathon ppt · hackathon pitch deck template · how to make hackathon presentation · hackathon ppt format The seven-slide hackathon deckTitle with the one-sentence problem and team nameThe user and the pain, one number if you have itThe demo, live, not a screenshotHow it works, one diagramWhat we cut and why, to show judgementWhat is next and what we needTeam and roles, with contact detailsThe seven-slide hackathon deck For Smart India Hackathon the format is more formal and the template is prescribed, but the same order inside it wins: problem, demo, how, next. Teams that open with a slide of technologies lose the room in the first fifteen seconds. How do I give a demo that works live? Freeze your code at least two hours before demos. Rehearse the exact click path three times on the machine you will present from, on the venue Wi-Fi if you can. Seed the data so the demo never depends on a live network call you do not control. Record a backup video of the full path and have it open in a tab. Assign one person to drive and one to talk. Also asked as: hackathon demo tips · how to demo at a hackathon · hackathon demo video · hackathon presentation tips · how to present a project in hackathon The demo that failed for us at STROT failed on a live API call over venue Wi-Fi. Every demo since has run on seeded data with a recorded fallback, and none has failed. How should a hackathon team be formed? Three people with three roles: one who builds the core, one who owns the interface and the data, one who owns the problem, the deck and the pitch and also tests everything. Decide roles before the event, not at hour one. A friend who cannot code but can research users and present is worth more than a fourth developer. Also asked as: hackathon team · how to form a hackathon team · hackathon team roles · how many people in a hackathon team · how to find hackathon team members · hackathon team size Every first prize we won was a team of three with those roles. Teams of five spend their first three hours negotiating and their last three merging conflicts. 3people on every team I wonwith36hours in a typical campushackathon3minutes you get to pitch2hours before demos to freezethe codeKey numbers What is Smart India Hackathon and how do I crack it? Smart India Hackathon is a national competition run by the Ministry of Education's Innovation Cell in which student teams solve problem statements posted by government ministries and industry. Teams register through their college, are shortlisted internally, then compete at the national level. To do well: pick a problem statement whose owner you can reach, build a working prototype early, and make the presentation about the ministry's outcome, not your stack. Also asked as: what is smart india hackathon · how to crack smart india hackathon · how to win smart india hackathon · how to register smart india hackathon · smart india hackathon problem statements · how smart india hackathon works · best project for smart india hackathon · sih 2026 · how to win sih hackathon The official portal carries the current year's problem statements, timeline and eligibility, and it changes each cycle, so read it rather than any summary, including this one [1]. What stays constant: the internal college round eliminates most teams, so treat the internal presentation as the real competition, and the national judges are domain experts from the problem's ministry, so the domain matters more than the demo polish. Do hackathons help your career or resume? Yes, when you turn them into evidence: a public repository with a readable README, a two-minute demo video, and a short write-up of the problem, the decision you made and the result. A line saying "participated in 6 hackathons" does nothing. A line saying "1st prize, Changethon 2025, IIT Roorkee, built a voice-first farming assistant over WhatsApp" with a link does the work of a semester of grades. Also asked as: hackathon resume · how to make resume for hackathon · how to add hackathon to resume · how to add hackathon certificate in linkedin · hackathon certificate · are hackathons worth it · do hackathons help get a job · hackathon vs internship On LinkedIn, add the hackathon under Honours &amp; awards with the issuer and date, and post the demo video the same week; hackathon posts travel further than any other student content, in my experience running a 500-member community. On the resume, one line per win, with the problem and the result, and the repository link. What mistakes make teams lose? Building for 34 hours and presenting for 2. Choosing a problem to impress rather than to solve. No roles, so everyone builds the same screen. A live demo that depends on Wi-Fi. A deck that opens with the tech stack. Not talking to a single real user. Sleeping zero hours and demoing incoherently. Every one of these is cheaper to avoid than to recover from. Also asked as: hackathon mistakes · why teams lose hackathons · hackathon tips and tricks · hackathon tips for beginners · how to prepare for a hackathon · hackathon strategy What separates the podium from the roomLEVEL 1Attendedshowed up, builtsomething, learned theformatLEVEL 2Finisheda working demo of onefeature, presented ontimeLEVEL 3Understoodtalked to a user, cutscope, explained theproblem before thesolutionLEVEL 4Rehearseddemo path frozen andpractised, backup videoreadyLEVEL 5Wonall of the above, plusone sharp insight statedin one sentenceWhat separates the podium from the room What should I do after the hackathon? Within a week: clean the repository, write the README, publish the demo video, and post the story. Within a month: decide whether the project deserves users, and if so, ship the smallest real version. Annapurna went from a hackathon prize to a tool people used because we kept the roles that worked and threw away the parts built for the judges. Also asked as: what to do after hackathon · turn hackathon project into startup · hackathon to startup · how to continue hackathon project · hackathon project after event From my carouselThree First Prizes, One Loss · 8 slides · full deck on Instagram and LinkedIn Can I invite a judge or mentor to my college hackathon? Yes. Organisers can reach me for judging, mentoring or a session on hackathon strategy before your event, on-site across India or remote. What I need from you is the date, the format, the problem statements if fixed, and the rubric you plan to use, or I will bring the four-criteria one above. Also asked as: hackathon judge invitation · how to invite a judge for hackathon · hackathon mentor · how to become a hackathon judge · hackathon judge requirements · hackathon speaker The details and the invite form are at pranjulrathour.scult.in/invite, and my email is pranjulrathour41@gmail.com. Free for student communities.

# RAG vs fine-tuning vs prompt engineering: which one your problem actually needs, with a decision tree and real costs
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/rag-vs-fine-tuning/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

RAG vs fine-tuning: what is the difference? RAG, retrieval-augmented generation, changes what the model reads: at answer time it retrieves passages from your documents and answers from them, with citations. Fine-tuning changes what the model is: it trains the weights on your examples so the model's behaviour, style, format or skill shifts permanently. RAG is for knowledge the model lacks or that changes. Fine-tuning is for behaviour no prompt can produce. They solve different problems, and the most common mistake is using one for the other's job. Also asked as: rag vs fine tuning · difference between rag and fine tuning · rag vs fine tuning llm · rag or fine tuning · is rag better than fine tuning · rag vs fine tuning which is better · retrieval augmented generation vs fine tuning · fine tuning vs rag for chatbot I built both kinds of system in the same six months of 2026: RAG.NextUpgrad, a production retrieval platform with hybrid search, reranking and a confidence gate [9], and FineTune Studio, a QLoRA fine-tuning platform with live telemetry and base-versus-tuned evaluation [10]. Clients asked me the same question about both, and this page is the answer I now give before writing any code. Knowledge or behaviour? Answer that in one word and you have chosen your architecture. Everything after is engineering. Pranjul Rathour When should I use RAG? When the answer depends on information the model does not have: your documents, your database, anything after its training cutoff, anything private. When answers must cite their source. When content changes often, because re-indexing a document takes seconds while retraining takes hours. When different users may see different documents, because retrieval can filter by permission and a model's weights cannot. When you need to ship this week, because a RAG prototype is an afternoon. Also asked as: when to use rag · rag use cases · why use rag instead of fine tuning · benefits of rag over fine tuning · rag for company documents · rag for customer support · rag for knowledge base · when is rag better Lewis et al. introduced the pattern for knowledge-intensive tasks precisely because a model's parameters are a poor place to store facts that must be exact and current [1]. Ovadia et al. compared knowledge injection by fine-tuning against retrieval directly and found retrieval consistently better at giving models new factual knowledge [3]. When should I use fine-tuning? When the problem is how the model behaves, not what it knows: a consistent voice, a strict output format, a domain's phrasing, a classification or extraction skill the base model does poorly, or a narrow task you want a small, cheap, fast model to do well. When you have hundreds to thousands of clean examples of the right output. When the requirement is stable enough that retraining every month would not be needed. When prompting with examples has been tried and still falls short. Also asked as: when to fine tune llm · fine tuning use cases · why fine tune instead of rag · benefits of fine tuning · fine tuning for style · fine tuning for structured output · fine tuning for classification · when is fine tuning better LoRA made this affordable by training small adapters instead of all weights [2], and LIMA showed how few examples alignment needs when they are clean: a thousand, not a hundred thousand [4]. Both papers point the same way: fine-tuning is a scalpel for behaviour, not a container for facts. Where does prompt engineering fit? First. A prompt is free to change, takes effect instantly and often solves the problem: a clear task, an output format, a few examples, a rule for the not-enough-information case. Few-shot examples in the prompt were the original demonstration that models can learn a task without training [7]. Every RAG system still needs a well-engineered prompt that says "answer only from these passages and cite them", and every fine-tuning project should start by proving that prompting was insufficient. Also asked as: rag vs fine tuning vs prompt engineering · prompt engineering vs fine tuning · prompt engineering vs rag · prompt engineering or fine tuning · few shot vs fine tuning · in context learning vs fine tuning · when is prompt engineering enough The order I insist on1Prompt: task, format,rules, tested on 20inputs2Few-shot: examples ofcorrect output in theprompt3Retrieval: the rightdocuments delivered asdata4Fine-tune: only forbehaviour thatsurvives all of theabove5Both: RAG for factsplus a small fine-tunefor voice or formatThe order I insist on The official prompting guides are free and current; read one before spending on anything else [8]. RAG vs fine-tuning: side by side The comparison, on the dimensions that decide real projects. Also asked as: rag vs fine tuning comparison · rag vs fine tuning pros and cons · rag vs fine tuning table · rag fine tuning differences · advantages and disadvantages of rag and fine tuning RAG versus fine-tuning versus promptingRAGFine-tuningPromptingWhat changesThe context the model readsThe model&#x27;s weightsThe instructionsSolvesMissing or changing knowledgeBehaviour, style, format,narrow skillsSteering and format, withinthe model&#x27;s abilitiesCitationsYes, per passageNoNoUpdate timeSeconds, re-index a documentHours, retrain and re-evaluateInstantAccess controlFilter documents per userImpossibleImpossibleUp-front costRetrieval engineering, indexDataset creation, GPU time,evaluationAlmost nonePer-query costHigher, more tokens in thepromptLower, shorter prompts,smaller model possibleDepends on prompt lengthHallucinationReduced when retrieval is goodUnchanged for factsUnchangedTypical failureWrong chunk retrievedForgetting, overfitting, stalefactsFragile phrasing across modelversionsTime to first versionAn afternoonDays to weeksMinutesRAG versus fine-tuning versus prompting Can I combine RAG and fine-tuning? Yes, and mature systems usually do. RAG supplies the facts; a fine-tune supplies the behaviour: the house voice, a strict answer format, better use of retrieved passages, or a smaller model that follows citation rules reliably. You can also fine-tune the embedding model or the reranker on your own query-passage pairs to improve retrieval itself. Add the fine-tune after the RAG system works and is measured, never before, so you can see what the training actually changed. Also asked as: rag and fine tuning together · combine rag with fine tuning · rag plus fine tuning · hybrid rag fine tuning · fine tune model for rag · fine tuning embeddings for rag · raft retrieval augmented fine tuning Is the problem knowledge, behaviour, or both?YESBoth. Build RAG first, measure recall andfaithfulness, then fine-tune a small model onexamples of good cited answers in your format.NOOne of them. Knowledge means RAG. Behaviourmeans fine-tuning, after prompting has beenexhausted.Is the problem knowledge, behaviour, or both? Can fine-tuning add knowledge to a model? Weakly, unreliably and expensively. A model fine-tuned on facts may repeat some of them, but it cannot cite them, it does not know when they changed, and it blends them with prior beliefs. Ovadia et al. found retrieval outperformed fine-tuning for injecting new knowledge, and that repeated exposure to facts was needed for fine-tuning to teach them at all [3]. Luo et al. document the forgetting that aggressive fine-tuning causes [5]. If the fact must be right and traceable, retrieve it. Also asked as: can fine tuning add knowledge · fine tuning for knowledge injection · does fine tuning teach new facts · fine tuning vs rag for knowledge · knowledge injection llm · fine tuning on documents This is the expensive mistake I see most: a team fine-tunes a model on their product manual, the manual changes, and the model confidently describes the old version with no way to show where it got it. Presenting to a room What does each approach cost? RAG costs are in retrieval engineering up front, chunking, embeddings, indexing, evaluation, and then per query, because every answer sends retrieved passages as tokens. Fine-tuning costs are up front in the dataset, weeks of a person's time to write and clean examples, plus a few GPU hours that are cheap or free, and then again with every requirement change. Per-query, a fine-tuned small model is cheaper than a large model with a long RAG prompt. Total cost depends on volume and how often things change. Also asked as: rag vs fine tuning cost · is fine tuning expensive · rag cost per query · fine tuning cost estimation · cheaper rag or fine tuning · llm cost rag · fine tuning roi Where the money goesRAGFine-tuningUp frontChunking, embedding, index, hybrid search,eval set: engineering daysDataset design and cleaning: weeks of aperson&#x27;s time, a few GPU hoursPer queryEmbedding call, retrieval, more prompt tokensFewer tokens, possibly a smaller modelWhen requirements changeRe-index, adjust prompt: hoursNew dataset, retrain, re-evaluate: daysMaintenanceIndex freshness, retrieval quality driftModel drift against changing needs, base modelupgradesHidden costRetrieval quality is hard to get rightEvaluation is hard to do honestlyWhere the money goes What are the failure modes of each? RAG fails when retrieval returns the wrong passage, when chunks lose context, when the prompt lets the model ignore the documents, or when passages conflict. Fine-tuning fails when the dataset is inconsistent, when the model overfits and memorises, when it forgets general ability, when the chat template is wrong, or when facts in the training data go stale. Prompting fails when phrasing breaks across model versions and when a task genuinely exceeds the model's ability. Each failure has a specific fix, and none of the fixes is "switch approaches" without measuring first. Also asked as: rag limitations · fine tuning limitations · problems with rag · problems with fine tuning · rag failure modes · fine tuning failure modes · catastrophic forgetting · rag hallucination Before you decide, answer theseIs the problem knowledge, behaviour or both?Have you tested a well-written prompt on 20 real inputs?Do the facts change more than once a quarter?Must answers cite a source?Do different users see different data?Do you have 300 or more clean examples of the right output?Is the requirement stable for six months?Have you measured where the current system fails?Before you decide, answer these Which is easier for a beginner or a student project? RAG. A retrieval system over documents you know is an afternoon to prototype, runs on a laptop with a free model API or a local model, and teaches chunking, embeddings, prompting, evaluation and hallucination in one project. Fine-tuning is a strong second project once you have a dataset you understand; QLoRA on a small model fits a free GPU. Doing both, and being able to say which problem each solved, is what interviewers want to hear. Also asked as: rag or fine tuning for beginners · easiest llm project · rag project for students · fine tuning project for students · should i learn rag or fine tuning first · genai project ideas 1question that decides thearchitecture2platforms I built to answerit, one for each20test inputs to proveprompting is not enough0cases where fine-tuning isthe right way to store factsKey numbers RAG vs fine-tuning interview questions Define both and state the one-line rule. Give an example that needs RAG, one that needs fine-tuning and one that needs both. Explain why fine-tuning is a poor way to add facts, citing forgetting and the inability to cite. Explain how you would prove prompting was insufficient before training. Estimate the cost shape of each. Describe a system you built and which approach it used, and why. Also asked as: rag vs fine tuning interview question · llm interview questions rag fine tuning · genai interview rag vs fine tuning · explain rag and fine tuning From my carousel7 Levels of RAG Apps · 9 slides · full deck on Instagram and LinkedIn Where to go from here Build the RAG version first, measure recall on twenty questions, and write down what it cannot do. That list is your fine-tuning specification, if you need one at all. My longer decision write-up with client examples is on the portfolio [11]. For a session at your college on choosing and building these systems, email pranjulrathour41@gmail.com or use pranjulrathour.scult.in/invite.

# Smart India Hackathon guide: how SIH works, how to register through your college, choose a problem statement, clear the internal round and present to ministry judges
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/smart-india-hackathon-guide/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

What is Smart India Hackathon? Smart India Hackathon is a nationwide competition organised by the Ministry of Education's Innovation Cell with AICTE and partners, in which student teams build solutions to problem statements posted by central and state government departments, public sector organisations and industry [1][2]. Teams register through their own college, go through an internal selection round, and shortlisted teams compete at the national level, where the problem statement's owners sit on the judging panels. It has software and hardware editions and runs on a months-long calendar. Also asked as: what is smart india hackathon · smart india hackathon meaning · what is sih · smart india hackathon explained · how smart india hackathon works · what happens in smart india hackathon · smart india hackathon in hindi · is smart india hackathon worth it · smart india hackathon 2026 Everything specific to a year, the dates, the number of problem statements, the team size rules, the prize amounts, changes each cycle and is published on the official portal [1]. This page is about the parts that do not change: how the structure works and what wins inside it. I have won three hackathons and lost one that taught me more, and I have judged and mentored at college events since. SIH is different from a weekend campus hackathon in two ways that decide everything: the judges own the problem, and the internal round is the real competition. At a campus hackathon you impress an engineer. At SIH you have to convince the person whose department will live with your solution. Build for the second person from day one. Pranjul Rathour How does Smart India Hackathon work, step by step? Problem statements are published on the portal. Your college registers as a participating institute and appoints a coordinator. Students form teams within the rules and register under the college. The college runs an internal hackathon to shortlist teams, typically a handful per problem statement it nominates. Shortlisted teams submit ideas through the portal, are evaluated, and the selected ones are invited to the grand finale, a multi-day build at a nodal centre, judged by the problem statement owners and experts. Also asked as: smart india hackathon process · sih process · how to participate in smart india hackathon · smart india hackathon steps · sih internal hackathon · sih rounds · how sih selection works · smart india hackathon timeline The SIH pipeline, in order1Problem statementspublished on theportal2College registers andnames a coordinator3Teams form within thesize and compositionrules4Internal collegehackathon shortliststeams5Nominated teams submitidea presentations viathe portal6Evaluation andselection for thegrand finale7Grand finale: build ata nodal centre, judgedby problem owners8Winners, and for manyteams, a path to pilotthe solutionThe SIH pipeline, in order The rules for team size, gender composition, mentor involvement and eligibility have varied between editions; the portal's current rules override anything you read elsewhere, including here [1]. How do I register for Smart India Hackathon? Registration runs through your institute, not directly as an individual. Find your college's SIH coordinator, often in the training and placement cell or the innovation cell, confirm the college is registered for the current edition, form your team within the rules, and register your team under the college on the portal by the deadline. If your college is not registered, the coordinator registers the institute first. Start this a month before the internal round, because approvals move at college speed. Also asked as: how to register smart india hackathon · smart india hackathon registration · sih registration process · sih registration 2026 · can i participate in sih individually · sih eligibility · who can participate in smart india hackathon · sih team size If your college has never participated, a small group of students taking the portal's institute registration page to the principal with the previous year's results usually gets it done. That is how many first-time colleges join. How do I choose a problem statement? Read the full statement, not the title, and answer four questions: who owns it and what outcome do they need; what data or systems does the solution depend on and can you get or simulate them; what is the constraint that makes it hard for the owner today; and can your team build a working prototype of the core in the time available. Prefer statements where you can reach a real user of the department's service. Avoid ones that need data you will never see. Also asked as: smart india hackathon problem statements · how to choose sih problem statement · best problem statement for smart india hackathon · sih problem statement selection · smart india hackathon topics · best topic for smart india hackathon · sih software edition problem statements · sih hardware edition Problem statement testYou can explain the department&#x27;s current process in three sentencesYou can name the person who would use the solution dailyThe data needed exists publicly, or can be realistically simulatedThe hardest technical part is something your team has done beforeA pilot in one district or one office is imaginableThe statement&#x27;s constraints, offline use, languages, low-end devices, are ones you can honourProblem statement test KrishGyan, which won Changethon at IIT Roorkee, came from exactly this reading of a problem: farmers who do not read or type, a voice-first assistant in their language over WhatsApp [4]. The same reading applies to ministry statements: find the constraint everyone else will ignore, and design for it. How do I clear the internal college round? Treat the internal presentation as the final, because for most teams it is. Bring a working prototype, even a thin one, not a slide deck. Open with the department's problem in its own words, demo the core in two minutes, show one architecture slide, then say what a pilot would look like. Practise the pitch with a timer. Ask the coordinator what the internal judges weigh and match it. Most internal panels eliminate on clarity and feasibility, not on ambition. Also asked as: how to crack smart india hackathon · how to win sih internal hackathon · sih internal round tips · sih ppt · sih presentation tips · how to get selected in sih · smart india hackathon tips · how to prepare for smart india hackathon What do SIH judges look for at the grand finale? The same four things every hackathon judge scores, weighted toward the owner's reality: feasibility, does it work and can it run in their environment; innovation, is there an insight about their problem; practicality, would their staff and citizens adopt it; and problem solving, did you understand the constraint. Ministry judges add a fifth: fit with existing systems and policy. Show that you know what the department already runs and how your solution attaches to it. Also asked as: sih judging criteria · smart india hackathon evaluation criteria · what judges look for in sih · sih grand finale judging · how sih projects are evaluated · sih rubric Those four criteria are the ones I put on screen when I brief a judging room, and the ones I have written about after sitting on panels [5][6]. At SIH the panel includes the people who wrote the statement, so the fifth criterion carries more weight than at any campus event. Pitching at CSJMU, Kanpur What should the SIH presentation contain? The portal prescribes a template for the idea submission; use it exactly. Inside it, the order that wins: the problem as the department experiences it, the proposed solution in one diagram, a working demo or a video of one, the technical approach with honest limits, feasibility and the constraints you honoured, the impact for the department and the citizen, and a pilot plan. Keep every slide readable from the back of a room. Also asked as: sih ppt template · smart india hackathon ppt · sih idea presentation · sih presentation format · best ppt for smart india hackathon · how to make sih ppt · sih idea submission The general pitch deck structure I recommend, adapted to whatever template the portal requires that year, is written up separately [7]. How do I build the prototype for SIH? Build the core workflow end to end first, with seeded or simulated data that looks like the department's, and make it demonstrable in three minutes. Honour the constraints in the statement, low bandwidth, regional languages, feature phones, offline use, from the first version, because that is where ministry judges look. Keep an architecture that could plausibly run inside government infrastructure. Add features only after the demo path is solid. Also asked as: sih prototype · how to build sih project · smart india hackathon project · sih project ideas · sih winning projects · sih tech stack · smart india hackathon software projects · sih project github How SIH teams progressLEVEL 1Registeredteam formed, statementchosen, portal doneLEVEL 2Internal finalista thin working prototypeand a clear pitchLEVEL 3Nominatedidea submission in thetemplate, honest scopeLEVEL 4Grand finalistfull demo on realisticdata, constraintshonouredLEVEL 5Winner or pilotthe department can seehow to run it next monthHow SIH teams progress What happens after Smart India Hackathon? Winners receive prizes, and in many cases the problem owner explores piloting or developing the solution further with the team; several past solutions have continued as products or government pilots. Whether you win or not, the project, the repository and the write-up are the durable result. Publish them, add the finale to LinkedIn under honours with the statement and department, and use the story in interviews. The line "grand finalist, Smart India Hackathon, problem statement from [department]" is understood by every Indian recruiter. Also asked as: what happens after sih · smart india hackathon prize money · sih winners · sih benefits · does sih help placement · sih certificate · smart india hackathon career benefits Prize amounts and post-event arrangements are set per edition on the portal [1]; do not rely on figures from earlier years. 4criteria every judge scores,plus fit with existing1internal round thateliminates most teams3minutes for the core demo,however long the slot1department user you must beable to nameKey numbers Common mistakes SIH teams make Choosing a statement by its title. Building for three months without ever showing a department user. Presenting the tech stack before the problem. Ignoring the constraint in the statement, offline, language, device, and getting caught in Q&amp;A. Six people with no roles. A demo that needs the venue's Wi-Fi. Reading the previous year's rules instead of this year's. Every one of these is avoidable with the checklists above. Also asked as: sih mistakes · why teams fail in sih · smart india hackathon mistakes to avoid · sih tips and tricks · sih strategy From my carouselThree First Prizes, One Loss · 8 slides · full deck on Instagram and LinkedIn Can you mentor or judge our SIH team or internal hackathon? Yes. I mentor teams on statement selection, scoping and the demo, and I judge and brief judging panels at college internal rounds, on-site across India or remote. # What are embeddings in AI? Text embeddings, vector similarity, choosing a model, and how embeddings power RAG and semantic search
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/what-are-embeddings-in-ai/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

What are embeddings in AI? An embedding is a list of numbers, a vector, that a model produces to represent the meaning of an input: a sentence, a paragraph, an image, a sound clip. The model is trained so that inputs with similar meaning produce vectors that are close together and dissimilar inputs produce vectors far apart. Once text is a vector, meaning becomes geometry: you can measure similarity with a distance, search by nearest neighbour, cluster, and feed vectors to other models. Also asked as: what are embeddings in ai · what is embedding in machine learning · what is text embedding · what is vector embedding · embeddings explained · what is an embedding model · embedding meaning in ai · what are embeddings in llm · word embeddings vs sentence embeddings Word2vec showed in 2013 that simple training objectives produce vectors where analogies work as arithmetic [1]. BERT produced contextual vectors for every token [2], and Sentence-BERT trained networks so that a whole sentence's vector could be compared with cosine similarity directly, which is the form every RAG system uses [3]. Dense passage retrieval then showed embeddings beating keyword search for question answering [4]. In every retrieval system I have built, the embedding model is chosen once, early, and it decides what "similar" means for the life of the index. This page is how I make that choice, and what I tell students who confuse embeddings with tokens. An embedding model is a definition of similarity, frozen into numbers. Pick the one whose idea of similar matches your users' idea of relevant. Pranjul Rathour How do embedding models work? A transformer reads the input and produces a vector for every token; a pooling step, usually the mean or a special token's vector, collapses them to one vector for the whole input; a final normalisation makes it unit length. Training uses pairs: a query and a passage that answers it, or two sentences that mean the same, pushed together, with unrelated pairs pushed apart, a contrastive objective. Millions of such pairs teach the model which differences matter and which do not. Also asked as: how do embeddings work · how are embeddings created · how embedding models are trained · contrastive learning embeddings · sentence transformers explained · how does text embedding work · embedding layer vs embedding model From text to a searchable vector1Tokenise the input2Run the transformer toget one vector pertoken3Pool to a singlevector, mean or aspecial token4Normalise to unitlength5Store with the textand its metadata6Compare at query timewith cosine similarityFrom text to a searchable vector Two terms collide here. An "embedding layer" inside any neural network maps token ids to vectors as the first step of processing; an "embedding model" is a whole network whose output is a vector for the input. The second is what RAG and search use. What is the difference between embeddings and tokens? Tokens are the pieces of text a model reads, word fragments mapped to integer ids; there are as many tokens as pieces. An embedding is one vector representing an entire input's meaning. A 500-word passage might be 650 tokens and exactly one embedding. Tokens are how language models consume text; embeddings are how retrieval systems compare it. People search for this distinction often because both are "numbers that represent text", and they are not the same numbers. Also asked as: embeddings vs tokens · are embeddings and tokens the same · difference between tokens and embeddings · token embedding vs sentence embedding · tokenization vs embedding · embeddings vs vectors · are embeddings and vectors the same thing Tokens versus embeddingsTokensEmbeddingsWhatInteger ids for text piecesA single vector for a whole inputHow many per passageHundredsOneProduced byA tokeniser, no learning at query timeAn embedding model, a neural networkUsed forFeeding text to an LLM, counting costSimilarity search, clustering, RAG retrievalComparable across modelsNo, vocabularies differNo, vector spaces differTokens versus embeddings What do dimensions mean, and how many do I need? Dimensions are the length of the vector, commonly 384, 768, 1,024 or 1,536, sometimes 3,072 or more. More dimensions can capture more nuance and cost more storage and search time. The right number is whatever your chosen model produces; it is not a knob to maximise. Matryoshka-trained models let you truncate a long vector to a shorter prefix with graceful quality loss, which is useful when storage matters [7]. Test truncation on your own retrieval set before relying on it. Also asked as: embedding dimensions · what is embedding dimension · how many dimensions for embeddings · 768 vs 1536 embeddings · embedding size · reduce embedding dimensions · matryoshka embeddings · embedding vector length A 1,536-dimension vector for a million chunks is about six gigabytes in 32-bit floats before any index overhead. A 384-dimension model is a quarter of that. Whether it retrieves worse for your documents is an empirical question, and it is often closer than the size suggests. How is similarity between embeddings measured? By a distance or similarity function between two vectors. Cosine similarity, the cosine of the angle between them, is the standard for text; on unit-length vectors it equals the dot product and ranges from minus one to one. Euclidean distance is common in image search. Use the metric the model's documentation specifies, normalise vectors at index time, and never mix metrics or models within one index. Also asked as: cosine similarity embeddings · how to compare embeddings · cosine similarity vs dot product · euclidean distance vs cosine similarity · embedding similarity score · what is a good cosine similarity score · semantic similarity There is no universal "good" cosine score. The same model can put unrelated texts at 0.6 and paraphrases at 0.85; another model spreads them differently. Thresholds come from your own labelled pairs, not from a blog post. Which embedding model should I use? Shortlist by the retrieval task on the MTEB leaderboard, filtered for your language and a size you can run [5][6]. Prefer models trained on query-to-passage pairs for RAG. Then evaluate two or three on twenty of your own questions against your own documents, measuring recall at k. Choose the smallest model that meets your target. For Hindi and mixed-language content, check multilingual models specifically; English-only leaders can collapse. Also asked as: best embedding model · best embedding model for rag · which embedding model to use · openai embeddings vs open source · best open source embedding model · best embedding model for semantic search · multilingual embedding model · embedding model for hindi · embedding model comparison · text-embedding-3 vs bge Choosing an embedding modelRetrieval score on MTEB for your language, not the overall averageTrained on query-passage pairs if the use is RAGMax input length covers your chunk sizeDimensions fit your storage and latency budgetRuns where you need it: API, GPU server, CPU, or browserLicence allows your useEvaluated on 20 of your own queries with recall at kModel name and version stored next to every vectorChoosing an embedding model The MTEB paper explains the benchmark's tasks and why a single average hides large differences between tasks [5]. Sentence Transformers is the library most open models ship with [10]; commercial APIs document their models and dimensions [11]. My own decision notes on switching models in a production RAG system are on the portfolio [13]. Pranjul Rathour How are embeddings used in RAG and semantic search? At index time, each document chunk is embedded and stored in a vector index. At query time the question is embedded with the same model and the nearest chunks are retrieved, then reranked and passed to the language model as context. Semantic search is the same retrieval without the generation step: the results are the chunks or documents themselves. Embeddings make "how do I reset my password" match a passage titled "Credential recovery" even though they share no words. Also asked as: embeddings in rag · how rag uses embeddings · semantic search with embeddings · embedding based search · vector search embeddings · how to use embeddings for search · embeddings for chatbot · semantic search vs keyword search Where embeddings help and where they failQuery typeEmbeddings aloneAdd keyword searchParaphrased questionExcellentNot neededExact product code orerror numberPoor, blurs into neighboursEssentialPerson or place nameWeakEssentialRare technical acronymWeakEssentialLong descriptive questionGoodHelps recallWhere embeddings help and where they fail That table is why every retrieval system I ship is hybrid: dense retrieval for meaning, BM25 for exact terms, fused with reciprocal rank fusion [12]. What else can I do with embeddings? Deduplicate near-identical documents by finding pairs above a similarity threshold. Cluster support tickets or feedback into themes. Classify text by nearest labelled examples, which needs no training run. Recommend items whose descriptions are close to what a user liked. Detect topic drift in a conversation. Match resumes to job descriptions by section. Anything that reduces to "which of these is most like that" is an embedding problem. Also asked as: embedding use cases · what can you do with embeddings · embeddings for classification · embeddings for clustering · embeddings for recommendation · embeddings for deduplication · applications of embeddings What are multimodal, image and code embeddings? Multimodal models place images and text in the same vector space, so a text query can retrieve images and an image can retrieve captions; CLIP established the approach [8]. Image embeddings power visual search and duplicate detection. Code embeddings, trained on code and natural language pairs, let you search a codebase by describing what a function does. Each is a separate model with its own space; a text embedding and an image embedding from unrelated models cannot be compared. Also asked as: image embeddings · multimodal embeddings · clip embeddings · code embeddings · audio embeddings · embeddings for images and text · visual search embeddings What are the limitations of embeddings? They compress meaning, so they lose detail, especially exact strings, numbers and negation: "no refund" and "refund" can land close. They inherit their training data's biases and domain, so a general model can misjudge medical or legal text. They are model-specific, so switching models means re-embedding everything. They cannot be reversed into the original text, which is a privacy advantage and an interpretability limit. Late-interaction methods such as ColBERT keep per-token vectors to recover some lost precision, at higher storage cost [9]. Also asked as: limitations of embeddings · problems with embeddings · embeddings and negation · embedding bias · can embeddings be reversed · embedding drift · when not to use embeddings 1embedding model per index,always20of your own queries isenough to compare models768dimensions in many strongopen models0reliable universalsimilarity thresholdKey numbers What are common embedding interview questions? Explain what an embedding is to a non-engineer. Explain why cosine similarity is used and why vectors are normalised. Compare tokens and embeddings. Describe how you would choose an embedding model for a RAG system and how you would evaluate it. Explain why keyword search is still needed. Say what happens when you switch models. If you have built one retrieval system, these are all stories rather than definitions. Also asked as: embedding interview questions · vector embeddings interview · rag interview questions embeddings · nlp interview questions embeddings From my carousel7 Levels of RAG Apps · 9 slides · full deck on Instagram and LinkedIn Where should I start with embeddings? Install Sentence Transformers, embed a hundred sentences you wrote, and print the nearest neighbours of a few. Then embed a real document set, ask twenty questions, and measure how often the right chunk is in the top five. Swap the model and measure again. That afternoon teaches everything above. If your college wants a hands-on session on retrieval, embeddings and RAG, email pranjulrathour41@gmail.com or use pranjulrathour.scult.in/invite.

# What is an AI agent? Agentic AI explained: tools, function calling, MCP, frameworks, and why most agents fail
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/what-is-an-ai-agent/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

What is an AI agent? An AI agent is a language model running in a loop with tools. Given a goal, the model decides on an action, your code executes it, a search, a database query, an API call, a file edit, the result is fed back, and the model decides the next action, until it judges the goal met or a stopping rule fires. The model supplies judgement; the tools supply reach; the loop supplies persistence. Without the loop it is a chatbot; without tools it is a planner that cannot act. Also asked as: what is ai agent · what is ai agents · what is an ai agent in simple words · ai agent meaning · ai agents explained · what is ai agent development · what is an llm agent · ai agent definition The pattern was named ReAct by Yao et al., reasoning and acting interleaved, with the model writing a thought, an action and reading an observation on each turn [1]. Toolformer showed models could learn when to call tools [2], Reflexion added self-critique between attempts [3], and the survey by Wang et al. maps the many variants that followed [4]. Anthropic's practitioner guide distinguishes fixed workflows, where code decides the steps, from true agents, where the model does, and argues for the simplest design that works [5]. I ship both kinds. My publishing pipeline is a workflow: code decides the order, models write the text. The coding assistant that helped build it is an agent: it reads, edits and runs tests until the tests pass. The distinction is the first thing to get right, because a workflow is cheaper, more predictable and easier to test, and most "agent" products are workflows that would be better admitted as such. Every agent I have built started as a workflow that needed one decision I could not write as an if-statement. That decision is where the model belongs. Everywhere else, write code. Pranjul Rathour What is agentic AI, and how is it different from generative AI? Generative AI produces content on request: text, images, code, audio. Agentic AI uses a generative model to pursue a goal through actions over multiple steps, using tools and reacting to results. The same model can do both; the difference is the harness around it. A chat window is generative. A system that reads your inbox, drafts replies, checks your calendar and books the meeting is agentic. Also asked as: what is agentic ai · what is agentic ai in simple words · agentic ai vs generative ai · what is generative ai and agentic ai · agentic ai meaning · agentic ai explained · difference between ai agent and agentic ai · agentic workflow Generative, workflow, agentGenerative AIAgentic workflowAutonomous agentWho decides the stepsNobody, one request oneresponseYour code, in a fixed orderThe model, at run timeUses toolsNoYes, in predetermined placesYes, chosen per stepPredictabilityHighHighLower, path varies per runCost per taskOne callA known number of callsUnknown until it stopsTestingCompare outputsTest each stepTest end-to-end taskcompletionBest forDrafting, summarising,translatingPipelines with clear stagesOpen-ended tasks withverifiable outcomesGenerative, workflow, agent How do AI agents work? Each turn, the agent's context holds the goal, the tool definitions, the history of previous actions and their results. The model reads it and outputs either a final answer or a tool call: the tool's name and arguments as structured data. Your code validates the call, runs the tool, appends the result to the context, and calls the model again. Guardrails sit around the loop: a maximum number of steps, a budget, permissions per tool, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Also asked as: how do ai agents work · how ai agents work · how to ai agents work · ai agent architecture · ai agent loop · how does an llm agent work · agent reasoning loop One turn of the agent loop1Assemble context:goal, tools, history,observations2Model outputs a toolcall or a final answer3Validate the callagainst the tool&#x27;sschema and permissions4Execute the tool andcapture the result5Append the observationto the history6Check stopping rules:done, step limit,budget, error7RepeatOne turn of the agent loop The whole loop is under a hundred lines in any language. The frameworks add memory management, retries, streaming, tracing and multi-agent orchestration on top; none of that changes the loop. What is tool calling or function calling? Tool calling, also called function calling, is the API feature that lets a model request an action in a machine-readable form instead of free text. You describe each tool with a name, a description and a JSON schema for its arguments. When the model decides a tool is needed it returns a call object with the tool name and arguments; your code runs the function and returns the result as a tool message. It is what makes agents reliable enough to build on, because you never parse prose to find the action. Also asked as: what is tool calling · what is function calling · what is function calling in llm · what is function calling in openai · tool calling vs function calling · how tool calling works · agent vs tool calling · llm tool use · structured outputs vs function calling The shape, in the form both major providers use [7][8]: { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;search_docs&quot;, &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Search the company knowledge base. Use for any question about policies or products.&quot;, &quot;input_schema&quot;: { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;object&quot;, &quot;properties&quot;: { &quot;query&quot;: {&quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot;, &quot;description&quot;: &quot;What to search for, in the user's words&quot;}, &quot;top_k&quot;: {&quot;type&quot;: &quot;integer&quot;, &quot;default&quot;: 5} }, &quot;required&quot;: [&quot;query&quot;] } } Two rules that decide whether the model picks the right tool: the description says when to use it, not just what it does, and the tools do not overlap. Ten tools with fuzzy boundaries produce worse agents than three tools with sharp ones. What is MCP, the Model Context Protocol? The Model Context Protocol is an open standard for exposing tools, data sources and prompt templates to AI applications through a common interface, so that a tool server written once can be used by any client that speaks the protocol, a coding assistant, a chat app, an agent framework, without a custom integration each time [6]. An MCP server declares its tools with schemas; the client lists them, the model calls them, the server executes. It turns "integrate this API with this agent" into "run this server". Also asked as: what is mcp model context protocol · mcp model context protocol tutorial · what is mcp in ai · mcp server explained · how does mcp work · mcp vs function calling · mcp vs api · how to build an mcp server · best mcp servers I run a public MCP server at tools.scult.in that exposes the same free tools and prompt library the website offers, so an agent can call the schema generator or pull a stamped prompt with one line of configuration and no signup [12]. Building it taught me the practical value of the protocol: the client side is finished by other people, so a server is the whole product. Function calling versus MCPFunction callingMCPWhat it isA model API feature for structured toolrequestsA protocol between an AI application and toolserversWho defines the toolsYour application, per model providerThe server, once, for any compliant clientPortabilityTied to your code and provider formatAny MCP client can use any MCP serverTransportInside the model API callStandard I/O or HTTP between processesRelationshipMCP servers are ultimately invoked through themodel&#x27;s function callingFunction calling is the mechanism, MCP is theplumbingFunction calling versus MCP How do I build an AI agent from scratch? Pick one task with a verifiable outcome, define one to three tools with tight descriptions and schemas, write the loop with a step limit and a budget, log every call, and run it on twenty real cases before adding anything. Only then decide whether it needs memory, more tools, a planner or a second agent. Most successful agents in production have fewer than five tools and a very clear stopping condition. Also asked as: how to build ai agents · how to build ai agents from scratch · how to build agentic ai · how to make ai agents · how to create an ai agent · build ai agent python · ai agent tutorial · how to build an ai agent without code The loop, in plain Python against a tool-calling API: def run_agent(goal: str, tools: dict, max_steps: int = 12) -&gt; str: history = [{&quot;role&quot;: &quot;user&quot;, &quot;content&quot;: goal}] for step in range(max_steps): reply = llm(history, tools=[t.schema for t in tools.values()]) if reply.tool_calls is None: return reply.text # final answer for call in reply.tool_calls: tool = tools[call.name] if tool.needs_confirmation and not confirm(call): return &quot;Stopped: action needs approval&quot; result = tool.run(**call.arguments) # validated by the schema history.append(tool_result(call.id, result)) log(step, call, result) return &quot;Stopped: step limit reached&quot; Everything a framework gives you is a refinement of those lines. Write them once yourself; you will debug every framework faster afterwards. Walking a room through the products he has shipped Which AI agent framework should I use? For a first agent, none: the loop above and your provider's SDK. When you need branching, retries, persistence and human-in-the-loop steps, LangGraph models the agent as a graph with explicit state and is the most widely used [9]. Provider SDKs from Anthropic and OpenAI now include agent loops and tool handling. For non-developers, n8n and similar automation tools wire models and APIs visually [11]. Choose by how much control you need over state and failure, not by popularity. Also asked as: best ai agent framework · langgraph vs crewai · langchain agents vs langgraph · autogen vs crewai vs langgraph · best framework for building ai agents · ai agent frameworks comparison · what is n8n ai agent · n8n vs make ai agent What are multi-agent systems? A multi-agent system splits a task across several agents with different tools or roles, a researcher, a writer, a reviewer, coordinated by a planner or a fixed handoff. It helps when the task decomposes cleanly and each part needs a different context, and it hurts when the coordination overhead, cost and failure surface outgrow the benefit. Start with one agent; move to several only when one agent's context or tool set becomes unmanageable. Also asked as: multi agent system · multi agent ai · multi agent vs single agent · ai agent orchestration · agent to agent communication · crewai multi agent · when to use multiple agents Anthropic's guide makes the same recommendation from a larger sample of deployments than I have: composable patterns first, prompt chaining, routing, parallelisation, orchestrator-workers, and autonomous agents only for open-ended problems where the model's judgement is needed at every step [5]. Why do AI agents fail? Agents fail for predictable reasons: the goal was vague, so the model optimised the wrong thing; too many overlapping tools, so it picked badly; no stopping rule, so it looped; a tool returned an error the model could not interpret; the context filled with history and it forgot the goal; it took an irreversible action nobody confirmed; or a document it read contained instructions and it followed them. Almost all of these are design failures, fixed in the harness rather than the model. Also asked as: why ai agents fail · ai agent problems · ai agents limitations · ai agent hallucination · are ai agents reliable · agent reliability · ai agents risks · ai agents challenges Guardrails every production agent needsA step limit and a token budget per taskPer-tool permissions, read-only by defaultHuman confirmation for send, delete, pay, publish and deployTool results treated as data, never as instructionsStructured logs of every call and resultA fixed evaluation set of real tasks, scored for completionTimeouts and retries with backoff on every toolA clear final-answer format so the caller can detect successGuardrails every production agent needs OWASP lists excessive agency and prompt injection among the top risks for LLM applications, and agents are where both bite hardest, because an injected instruction can now cause an action, not just a bad sentence [10]. What is agent memory? Agent memory is whatever the agent can consult beyond the current context: the conversation so far, a scratchpad of notes it writes to itself, a vector store of past interactions or documents it can retrieve from, and structured facts in a database. Short-term memory is the context window; long-term memory is retrieval. Most agents need less memory than their builders assume and more discipline about what to forget. Also asked as: ai agent memory · long term memory for ai agents · short term vs long term memory llm · agent memory architecture · how do ai agents remember · vector database for agents Are AI agents worth learning, and what jobs use them? Yes. Agents are how language models get connected to real systems, and every AI engineering role I see in 2026 expects familiarity with tool calling, at least one orchestration pattern and the safety basics. Learn them by building one that does a job you actually have, connect it to a real API, and measure how often it finishes the task. That measured number, on a public repository, is worth more than any course certificate. Also asked as: should i learn ai agents · why learn ai agents · how long to learn ai agents · roadmap to learn ai agents · ai agents course · best ai agents course · agentic ai salary in india · agentic ai roadmap · ai agent developer I will not quote an "agentic AI engineer salary" because I have no measured source for one; job posts in India in 2026 mostly list it under AI engineer or GenAI engineer roles, and pay tracks those roles in the same city and company tier. How agent skills usually developLEVEL 1Chatprompt a model well andread its outputcriticallyLEVEL 2Toolconnect one function witha tight schema and testitLEVEL 3Loopwrite the agent loop withlimits and logsLEVEL 4Harnesspermissions,confirmations, evaluationset, tracingLEVEL 5SystemsMCP servers, multi-agenthandoffs, cost control inproductionHow agent skills usually develop 3tools or fewer in mostagents that work in12step limit I start with20real tasks in the firstevaluation set1MCP server I run, free, attools.scult.inKey numbers What are common AI agent interview questions? Explain the agent loop and where the model's judgement is actually needed. Compare a workflow with an agent and say when you would choose each. Describe how tool calling works and how you write a tool description. Explain how you would stop an agent from taking a harmful action, and how you would measure whether it works. Describe a failure you debugged. If you have built even one agent with a real tool, you can answer all five.
